title: macOS 27 Golden Gate now available, here is everything new
snippet: After months of beta testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now rolling out to everyone, bringing Apple’s new Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, major Safari additions, and a long list of performance and quality-of-life improvements. Here’s everything new. more…
fullText:
After months of beta testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now rolling out to everyone, bringing Apple’s new Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, major Safari additions, and a long list of performance and quality-of-life improvements. Here’s everything new.

During this year’s WWDC, Apple presented its operating systems somewhat differently than users and developers were used to.

Rather than introducing new features for each platform individually, Apple spent relatively little time on each operating system and focused much of the event on cross-platform features and improvements, largely because many of them rely on the new Apple Intelligence framework.

That said, macOS 27 Golden Gate still includes several welcome improvements of its own, both in design and functionality, starting with some much-needed tweaks to Liquid Glass.

Liquid Glass and UI improvements

While macOS Tahoe 26 featured Apple’s revamped look, it fell short visually compared to other systems, particularly iOS 26 and iPadOS 26.

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple spent some time further integrating the new Liquid Glass into the system, while also bringing over some of the visual tweaks introduced in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. That includes a new Liquid Glass slider, which lets users customize just how transparent or opaque they want the effect to be.

The Liquid Glass appearance setting also includes a fun little easter egg featuring Clarus the Dogcow, which appears when you scroll the demo pane all the way down, and then keep going.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also introduces revamped app icons, more in tune with the Liquid Glass look, with additional layers that add depth and detail across light, dark, tinted, and all-clear global system settings.

The same goes for the revamped traffic light buttons Apple introduced midway through the beta period. Rather than the old flat green, yellow, and red controls, they now feature a Liquid Glass look, complete with a playful bouncing effect when users click (or perhaps, soon, touch?) and drag them before letting go.

Another welcome interface improvement in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Apple’s decision to standardize the corner radius across system windows and apps, rather than making it dynamic based on the UI elements present in a window’s menu bar.

Although Apple’s intentions were deliberate, many assumed the inconsistent corner radii were a bug, prompting Apple to specifically call attention to the change during the WWDC keynote.

An equally divisive design decision Apple rolls back with macOS 27 Golden Gate is the sheer number of icons shown alongside menu items. With macOS 26 Tahoe, Apple added symbols next to nearly every command across its apps, an attempt to make menus more visually descriptive that instead drew criticism for making them busier and, in some cases, harder to scan.

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has (thankfully) reversed course, removing most of those icons and returning menus to a cleaner, less visually cluttered look.

Other visual tidbits in macOS 27 Golden Gate include edge-to-edge sidebars and more distinct active windows, both of which were also divisive in macOS Tahoe 26.

Siri AI and the new Siri app

This is perhaps the most significant new feature of macOS 27 Golden Gate. Apple’s revamped Siri, developed in partnership with Google’s Gemini model, gets its own app, in addition to an in-depth, system-wide integration.

The new Siri AI leverages a new per-device indexing system for the user’s data and lives in both Spotlight and the new Siri app.

The Siri app looks and works just as users are mostly used to with other AI assistant apps: a left-hand panel lists the user’s chat history across all compatible platforms, while the main chat panel lets the user type in prompts, attach images and files, or dictate to start a voice-based conversation. The app also supports search and pinned conversations, which is a nice plus depending on the user’s workflow.

The new Siri AI can pull information from the web and the user’s context to provide useful, actionable answers. During the beta period, the new Siri received overwhelmingly positive feedback, even though it can sometimes be slower than users accustomed to other LLM-powered AI assistants expect.

Another useful ability of the new Siri AI is its ability to interact with native and third-party apps, in addition to taking actions directly, taking the app integration available with the old Siri significantly further.

Importantly, developers need to expose their apps’ content and capabilities through the App Intents framework, so expect this aspect of the new assistant to improve over time as more developers update their apps for macOS 27 Golden Gate.

Finally, there is a systemwide “Ask Siri” option in context menus that lets users select text, images, or files and ask Siri about them directly. For example, users can Control-click an image in a document and ask Siri to help them learn more about it, or select a portion of text and ask Siri to rewrite it, proofread it, change its tone, or provide feedback on the writing.

Siri AI is available in English at launch, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish coming in October. For now, Siri AI won’t be available in China or in the EU due to regulatory issues.

Apple Intelligence

We went in-depth on Apple’s new foundation models here, but the gist is that for its 2027 OS releases, the company developed a new version of its Apple Intelligence models. Here’s Apple on each one:

AFM 3 Core, the next generation of our 3-billion-parameter dense model that delivers a step up in quality.

AFM 3 Core Advanced, our most powerful on-device model. It’s natively multimodal, enabling helpful features like expressive voices and higher-accuracy dictation. Built on cutting-edge Apple research, this 20-billion-parameter model uses a sparse architecture, activating just 1 to 4 billion parameters at a time depending on the request. AFM 3 Core Advanced is unlocked by and optimized for our most capable Apple silicon systems.

AFM 3 Cloud, our server-side workhorse, optimized for speed, efficiency, and performance.

ADM 3 Cloud (Image), for image generation and editing, which unlocks advanced photo-editing tools, the all-new Image Playground, and more.

AFM 3 Cloud Pro, our most capable server-based model, which powers our most demanding use cases, like agentic tool use and complex reasoning.

In practice, macOS 27 Golden Gate leverages two local models, AFM 3 Core and AFM 3 Core Advanced, while the other models are cloud-based. The performance of these two local models depends on the Mac’s hardware, particularly how much memory it has available to run their active parameters and other AI workloads.

When it comes to how Apple Intelligence is implemented in macOS 27 Golden Gate, it is somewhat of a mixed bag. The models themselves are quite good for everyday tasks, such as getting help to draft an e-mail, proofreading a document, or summarizing text.

The problem is that Apple is currently going somewhat overboard on how and when Siri AI is presented to the user, which can sometimes be a bit overwhelming or get in the way of what the user is trying to accomplish.

One great Apple Intelligence addition to macOS 27 Golden Gate is a new Visual Intelligence shortcut. By pressing Command-Shift-Space, users can select any region of the display and immediately ask Siri about it. That works with images, PDFs, text, or just about anything else shown on screen.

Alas, not every macOS 27-compatible Mac will run the new Apple Intelligence, which requires an A18 Pro, M1, or later chip. Here’s Apple’s official list of Macs that support the new features:

MacBook Neo (2026)

MacBook Air with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

MacBook Pro with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

iMac with Apple silicon (2021 and later)

Mac mini with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

Mac Studio (2022 and later)

Mac Pro with Apple silicon (2023)

Most Apple Intelligence features are available in the same languages supported by the current version of Apple Intelligence, including Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Apple Intelligence is currently unavailable in China due to regulatory issues. Additionally, Apple says there will be usage limits for certain Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features, although the company has yet to share specific details on that.

Performance and reliability improvements

During the WWDC26 keynote, Apple highlighted dozens upon dozens of improvements coming to all its operating systems.

On macOS 27 Golden Gate, this means faster AirDrop transfers, improved network file browsing, faster Spotlight indexing (particularly for shortcuts and actions), and faster iCloud Photos uploads with selective priority syncing.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also improves Safari and Calendar scrolling, as well as the animations in Mission Control and Spaces. Apple also tweaked Mail indexing and search, as well as the underlying system for Spotlight suggestions.

Other tidbits include improved window position consistency and persistence across external displays, HDR support for system UI elements, a broader range of high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes for external monitors, and more complete touch support in Sidecar, including tapping controls, one-finger scrolling, system gestures, and Markup.

Safari

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces Notify Me, a new Safari feature that can monitor webpages and alert users to relevant changes, such as price drops, product restocks, event registrations opening, or virtually anything else they ask it to track.

Notify Me can check for changes hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly, with additional options to specify the days of the week and times when those checks should run.

Additionally, Safari on macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces “Describe an Extension,” which lets users create extensions using natural language.

To help users get started, Apple provides several examples across productivity, focus, creativity, and design and development. Users can also simply describe what they need in their own words and let Apple Intelligence handle the rest.

Both features can be accessed from the “More Options” hamburger menu on the right side of the active Safari tab.

For users who tend to open way too many tabs as the day progresses, Safari can now automatically organize and group tabs together based on topic.

Another interesting tidbit in Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate is the new pull-to-refresh gesture, which, like on iOS and iPadOS, lets users refresh the page by swiping down past the rubber-band effect.

This gesture is also available in other system apps, such as Mail, News, and Calendar, which many see as further foreshadowing of touchscreen Macs rumored to be announced as early as this year.

iPhone Mirroring

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, users can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window to different aspect ratios, a change many saw as an early sign that Apple was preparing the feature for a foldable iPhone.

Well! You can now resize iPhone Mirroring to ANY size! (on an iOS 27-compiled app)

Foldable iPhone is so coming LOL

it doesn't switch to iPad layout though, which is weird… now I am scared for foldable iPhone pic.twitter.com/B9hjxuXWH5

— Dylan (@DylanMcD8) June 8, 2026

Now that the iPhone Duo is official, Mac users can get an early taste of what that experience will look like. Alas, Apple notes that iPhone Mirroring remains unavailable in the European Union.

Shortcuts

This is perhaps one of the most useful additions to Apple Intelligence in Apple’s OS updates this year.

Despite its relatively approachable take on automation, Shortcuts can still feel intimidating to more casual users. Now, users can simply describe what they want to accomplish, and Apple Intelligence will build it as a native shortcut.

To help users get started, the Shortcuts app also highlights several suggestions on the new shortcut creation screen, including:

Dictate and translate to Spanish

Write a weather forecast haiku

Play my exercise playlist when I arrive at the gym

Create a recipe from these leftovers

Summarize my day every morning

Prioritize my to-do list every morning

When I get in the car, get directions

Dictate my idea and save it to the clipboard

Dim screen brightness when Bedtime begins

Turn on Do Not Disturb when I open the TV app

As a side note, if you’d like to get deeper into Shortcuts, make sure to follow Stephen Robles’s fantastic work on YouTube and on Instagram. Also, check out Shortcuts Playground, from MacStories, an even more powerful natural-language-based shortcut creation tool.

Photos

The Photos app now offers three Apple Intelligence-powered editing tools: an enhanced version of Clean Up, which removes objects, people, or other undesired elements from photos; Extend, which generates the surrounding area of an image in case the user decides the original photo is too cropped-in; and Spatial Reframing, which lets users change the angle and composition of a photo after it has been taken.

Additionally, iCloud Shared Albums now supports full-resolution sharing and lets Windows and Android users join in via iCloud.com.

Other new features include playing any set of photos and videos as a slideshow with custom music, transition styles, and duration, photo ratings with a new star system, and a new, dedicated “Captured by Me” collection.

More macOS 27 Golden Gate tidbits

Calendar lets users add, edit, or update events by describing them.

Finder can now intelligently suggest file and folder names, based on their contents.

Image Playgrounds expands support for different styles, and leverages a new foundation model for even better results

Maps gets an enhanced Flyover experience with improved textures, more details, and sharper rendering for hundreds of cities around the world.

Messages now (finally) consolidates tapback notifications and improves syncing across devices.

*Notes supports trackpad-handwritten notes and sketches, expands Markdown support with copy/paste, and adds Section Links.

Podcasts now supports video podcasts, complete with support for picture and picture playback.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also marks the final release to support Rosetta. As Apple explains, “only apps will no longer run on Mac computers with Apple silicon after this update,” and you can read more about that here.

Compatibility

According to Apple’s official list, macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with the following Macs:

title: Valve is still figuring out ‘how and when’ to do Steam Deck 2
snippet: Now that Valve has finally launched its entire 2026 hardware lineup - the Steam Controller, the Steam Machine, and today's Steam Frame - are we any closer to a next-gen Steam Deck handheld? Valve isn't saying so yet. The company is figuring out "how and when we can deliver something like that," Valve designer Pierre-Loup Griffais now tells IGN. Valve has been clear for years that 1) a Steam Deck 2 will indeed happen, and 2) it's not coming until Valve finds the right chip. The original Steam Deck worked because it delivered the right combination of price, performance, and battery life, and Valve has repeatedly said it won't sacrifice effici … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Now that Valve has finally launched its entire 2026 hardware lineup — the Steam Controller, the Steam Machine, and today’s Steam Frame — are we any closer to a next-gen Steam Deck handheld? Valve isn’t saying so yet. The company is figuring out “how and when we can deliver something like that,” Valve designer Pierre-Loup Griffais now tells IGN.

Valve has been clear for years that 1) a Steam Deck 2 will indeed happen, and 2) it’s not coming until Valve finds the right chip. The original Steam Deck worked because it delivered the right combination of price, performance, and battery life, and Valve has repeatedly said it won’t sacrifice efficiency in the sequel.

“We also don’t want more performance to come at a significant cost to power efficiency and battery life,” Griffais told me in 2023, saying he wanted to see a “leap” instead — but suggesting that leap might not be physically possible for another couple of years.

Earlier this year, Valve got my hopes up that the wait for a chip was over — when Griffais revealed the team was “hard at work” on the next Steam Deck gaming handheld in an interview with IGN. He wouldn’t say when it might happen. I assumed that was caution, because RAMageddon had already pushed the company to delay and reprice the Steam Machine and Steam Frame headset by then.

Today, IGN’s new question was: “Has the current hardware shortage impacted the way Valve is thinking about actually putting a Steam Deck 2 into development?” Griffais’ immediate answer was “Not really.”

That could be good news for impatient gamers — or it could mean that the company will wait out RAMageddon before it dares intercept the silicon supply chain again. Valve originally wanted to build a “far more affordable” headset, for instance, but instead it faced brutal RAM negotiations to eventually arrive at a $1,059 price tag.

The real question is: Has Valve yet identified the future chip that will appear in the Steam Deck 2? Because the company will work backwards from that chip’s availability to create the hardware it lives within.

Intel’s Panther Lake handheld chip in the MSI Claw 8 EX AI Plus is the first I’ve tried that comes close to the kind of “generational leap” that Griffais has been talking about, but Panther Lake handhelds are incredibly expensive, and the Intel chip wasn’t a silver bullet in my tests. But I bet Valve has seen the future of Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm chips, and maybe a future one will do the trick.

I hope a Steam Deck 2 will kick-start a new golden age of handheld gaming; I fear it may cost too much for that.

title: Amazon Prime Video takes on TikTok with short-form news clips
snippet: Prime Video is adding on-demand local and national news clips as Amazon joins other streamers experimenting with short-form video to capture younger viewers.
fullText:
Amazon Prime Video is coming after TikTok with the addition of short-form news clips. The company said on Monday that it’s expanding its news coverage to include on-demand news clips offering both local and national stories. These will be available on TVs and other living room devices, but will soon roll out to the web and Prime Video’s mobile apps, the company said.

The clips will be available in the News destination within the Prime Video app in its Trending Topics and the Local News carousels. They join Prime Video’s existing local, national, and world news coverage from a number of major providers, which are available to everyone in the U.S. regardless of whether they have a Prime subscription.

Amazon could not yet confirm whether the clips on mobile would be oriented for vertical video or not, only that they would be considered short-form content on iOS and Android.

While TikTok is better known as an entertainment destination, it’s also, along with Instagram, increasingly a place where younger people get their news. Gen Z in particular often watches news creators and influencers on short-form apps, including YouTube Shorts. Amazon, which doesn’t have a true social destination of its own, is instead adding short-form video to Prime Video, in hopes of capturing Gen Z’s attention.

But Gen Z viewers are drawn to these social apps not necessarily because of the length of the clips, but rather because of how the information is presented. Based on findings from Pew Research, these younger news consumers want short-form news content that “feels organic, not over-produced.”

Prime Video is not the first streamer to add short-form clips to its content lineup. Peacock added support for short-form clips in March, followed by HBO Max and Netflix in July, then Disney+ in August. Combined, the updates represent an industrywide effort to meet viewers where they are — which is now often looking for entertainment in shorter bursts and consumable in moments or minutes instead of portions of hours or longer.

title: Here’s what’s new with parental control features in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27
snippet: Included in today’s 2027 system updates from Apple are several new Screen Time and parental control features aimed at giving parents more control over how their kids use their devices. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Included in today’s 2027 system updates from Apple are several new Screen Time and parental control features aimed at giving parents more control over how their kids use their devices. Here are the details.

Today’s updates include important parental control improvements

Apple today released iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 with what it describes as a “new suite of powerful, intuitive, and easy-to-use tools that helps parents create safer digital experiences for their kids,” many of which the company previewed in June, during the WWDC26 keynote.

In essence, the new features focus on four areas: what content kids can access, who they can communicate with, when they can use their devices, and how parents can manage those controls.

All of them fall under the protections and restrictions of Child Accounts, which Apple says are required for children under 13, or the equivalent minimum age in their country or region, and available for children up to 18.

With iOS 27, Apple has also simplified the setup process for new Child Accounts. Parents can start with a small set of essential apps, a recommended starter set, or choose exactly which Apple apps their child can access from the outset.

Once a parent sets up a Child Account, they can choose which apps and websites their child can access, as well as set age and content restrictions for movies, TV shows, music, books, and other media.

Parents can now also rely on Ask to Browse, a feature that lets kids request access to blocked websites in Safari across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with parents approving requests in Messages. This is similar to Ask to Buy, which already requires parental approval before children can download apps or make in-app purchases.

Parents can also require kids to ask for approval before connecting with new contacts, set shared or individual daily limits for categories such as Entertainment, Games, and Social Media, and create schedules that determine which apps are available at different times of day. Those schedules can also vary depending on the day of the week.

Screen Time itself has also been redesigned, with a new architecture that Apple says makes parental controls sync more quickly across devices in a Family Sharing group. Parents can now see weekly usage summaries and their kids’ most-used apps at a glance, temporarily pause access to a device, open things back up for a limited period, and quickly switch between different schedules.

Communication Safety is also expanding beyond nudity detection. The feature can now block detected gore or violent content in shared images and videos, while displaying a warning and additional resources.

Time Allowances are also more flexible. Parents can create their own app categories, move apps between them, and assign a time allowance as soon as they approve a new app through Ask to Buy. Websites associated with an app can also automatically follow the same allowance.

Apple says its suggested Time Allowances are based on a child’s age and expert research. The company is also working with the American Academy of Pediatrics to adapt its Family Media Plan into guidance for parents using Apple products.

Finally, Apple notes that all devices in a Family Sharing group need to be running the version 27 software releases to use the new Screen Time experience.

title: Hands-on: Nothing’s $25 CMF Buds Neo are way better than the price suggests
snippet: Last month, Nothing’s CMF brand launched a new pair of $25 earbuds in the CMF Buds Neo. Too good to be true, I figured, but after getting my hands on them, I’m pleasantly surprised by what they bring to the table despite some expected downsides. more…
fullText:
Last month, Nothing’s CMF brand launched a new pair of $25 earbuds in the CMF Buds Neo. Too good to be true, I figured, but after getting my hands on them, I’m pleasantly surprised by what they bring to the table despite some expected downsides.

The CMF Buds Neo bring a lot to the table on paper. 52-hour battery life, active noise cancellation, some flashy colors, and even dual-device connections alongside support for the Nothing X app and EQ presets. For $25, it’s a compelling package. 

How does it deliver in real life?

I’ve spent a few hours listening to CMF Buds Neo and, honestly, I’m pretty impressed!

	

At their core, they get the job done. The earbuds have decent sound quality, though they’re a bit hollow on default settings. I found that turning down the bass enhancement improves the sound quality, and they’re more optimized for speech (podcasts, etc) than music. Nothing Ear (3a) sound far better; don’t get me wrong, but probably not 4x better as the price on paper suggests.

The sound quality is the most important thing here when the price is so low, and it’s certainly more than good enough to make these a good deal. And there’s clearly more weight put in the price than anything else. CMF Buds Neo have some clear and obvious downsides. The case is cheap-feeling despite looking very nice, and the same goes for the earbuds – the materials feel cheap, but they fit nice in my ear and stay comfortable over a few hours of use. The touchpads on the earbuds are responsive, but lack a play/pause gesture by default. Another downside is the range, as I found these disconnect from my Fold 8 more quickly than other earbuds I’ve tested in recent memory. The case magnets that hold the earbuds in place work well, and there are some nice touches such as a snappy hinge and the lanyard hole on a rotating corner piece. 

There’s also no pairing button on the case, something that will never fail to annoy me, but at least there’s Google Fast Pair – humorously, the Fast Pair pop-up lacks a picture of the earbuds and just says “blue” on the variant I bought.

Downsides are aplenty here, which really shouldn’t come as a surprise. But, at the core, you’re getting earbuds that sound good enough, have most important features, and cost just $25. If you need a spare pair of earbuds to throw in a backpack or at your bedside, or a daily driver on a budget, these are a winner in my book.

title: Traveling to China? Here Are the Apps You’ll Need to Survive
snippet: Forget everything you think you know about China’s internet and read this first.
fullText:
So, you’re going to China and you need to get your phone in order, but you don’t know where to start. That was me, a month ago.

Now I’ve been there, for a week of work and another week of personal travel in and around Shenzhen. In that time, I got a good grasp on the ecosystem of apps and mini-apps. Enough, at least, to get you started if you’re venturing to China anytime soon.

Most people will be aware – but I’ll say it here just in case you’re not – that many US-based apps and services aren’t available in China, thanks to the Great Firewall (a series of laws that limits and regulates internet use). This affects the availability of Western social media such as Instagram and the non-Chinese version of TikTok, messaging apps including WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger, and anything that falls under the sprawling Google umbrella.

If you use an eSIM to roam while you’re in China (highly recommended), or manage to get a VPN to work reliably (not a given), you’ll still be able to access those services. But you will also need a whole different set of apps – and this isn’t optional. You won’t get by for a single day without them.

I’d been to China once before, over a decade ago. Unprepared for the Great Firewall and unaware of the workarounds, I just went offline for a week.

Now, that’s not an option – in large part because if you want to pay for anything in China, you must do so using your phone. I didn’t take a credit card out with me for the whole two weeks I was in the country. Anywhere else, this would have been reckless, but in China, I simply wouldn’t have been able to use it.

WeChat and Alipay: The super apps

Enter WeChat and Alipay. They’re super apps, meaning you can do all kinds of things with them, but you’ll mainly need them for payments. I would strongly recommend downloading both and setting them up by linking them to multiple credit cards before you arrive in China (it can be trickier to do once you’re in the country).

To pay for things, from groceries to public transit, you’ll either scan a QR code with your phone, or allow the vendor to scan your personal QR code. 

I recommend having both apps because occasionally one of the apps didn’t play ball when I was trying to pay for something (a stressful experience if that something was a dinner I’d already eaten), but the other would work just fine.

Alipay and WeChat are known as super apps because they’re platforms that host thousands of lightweight mini applications that sit inside them – from popular drinks brands such as Hey Tea and Luckin, to the transit app that allowed me to order KFC straight to my seat on a high-speed train from a station we passed through.

Just a snapshot of WeChat’s mini app universe.Katie Collins/CNET

Some apps, such as Meituan (for food delivery) and Didi (for ride-hailing and, which I’ll address separately later) worked best for me as mini-apps within WeChat and Alipay. Not all mini apps are designed for payment, but this is almost exclusively what I used the super apps for.

Of the two, I preferred using Alipay, largely because I found the interface easier to navigate. Whenever I opened the app, the home screen presented me with three big buttons titled “Scan,” “Pay/Receive” and “Transport,” which allowed me immediate access to public transit tickets and passes for whatever city I was in.

I found Alipay marginally easier to navigate.Katie Collins/CNET

The option to translate the content of mini apps was also less fiddly to find on Alipay, popping up as a little tab on the left of the screen.

Where Alipay and WeChat differ – and another reason I’d recommend having both – is that WeChat is first and foremost a messaging app. When you open the app, the first thing that pops up will be your chat history, just as if you were looking at your messages.

You might not know anyone in China right now, but your hotel will probably want to add you on WeChat – probably ahead of your stay – in order to have an open line of communication with you in which messages can be easily translated between languages. I found this super helpful for arranging transfers and breakfast, among other things.

I also thought WeChat did a better and more consistent job of translating mini app content overall (top tip: tap the three dots in the top right corner of the screen to access the hidden menu containing the translation option).

Amap: The Google Maps alternative

Perhaps the biggest challenge for me while traveling through China – digitally speaking, at least – is what it did to Google Maps. Overnight it turned from a geographical safety blanket that’s guided me around the world multiple times into the most useless app on my phone.

Katie Collins/CNET

Thanks to my eSIM, I could access Google Maps, but it contains almost none of the location information about China you’ll actually need. Some people suggested using Apple Maps as an alternative, but I didn’t find it much better.

Instead, I recommend doing as the Chinese do and downloading Amap. I found it frustratingly slow to load at times, and it didn’t have the same depth of information Google Maps has about dining establishments – the lack of menus is a big difference, for example. But if you want to find local businesses and walk around without getting lost, Amap is the one.

One nice touch is that it would plan out walking routes for me based on tree cover and shade provided by buildings depending on the time of day. Given that the temperature was regularly over 100 degrees Fahrenheit with high humidity, I appreciated this guidance.

Didi: The Uber alternative

You might think, like I did when I first landed in China, that you’ll probably take public transit everywhere. Then you’ll see the price of a Didi and reconsider.

If you can use Uber (which is not available), you can use Didi – it’s straightforward, affordable and convenient. You can download it separately, but I used it as a mini app within Alipay, which made it easy to pay. 

One quirk was that it didn’t automatically take the money from my card after I finished a journey. Instead, I had to manually pay after getting out of the vehicle. I often forgot to do this, but you’re not allowed to book another trip until you’ve paid for your last one. The app also prompted me to pay for my journey to the airport up front, which I appreciated, as I would’ve hated to accidentally skip town without paying.

Something to know about Didi is that the driver will confirm you’re the correct passenger by asking you the last four digits of your phone number. To overcome the language barrier, I found the best strategy was to have the last four digits saved in my notes app and to have it open to show the driver every time I jumped into a car.

Trip.com: The only booking app you’ll need

Are you an Expedia or Booking.com loyalist? Forget them both. You need one app and one app only for booking hotels in China, and that’s Trip.com.

Trip.com has a much bigger portfolio of accommodation in China than any other site or service you might use. If you’re an avid reader of reviews, you’ll also find many, many more here than anywhere else on the internet.

The app also serves as a portal for booking almost anything else you might want or need while you’re in China. I used it to book high-speed train tickets, entry to attractions and even a theater excursion. (Yes, I went to the theater, and no, I didn’t understand a word.)

Some people have also recommended Klook for booking tickets and excursions, but I can’t recommend it personally as I didn’t use it. I also liked the fact that Trip.com displayed all of my tickets and bookings in a chronological itinerary.

Rednote: For inspo

The decline of travel journalism and blogs means that many of us turn to Instagram and TikTok for inspiration when going on trips these days. You can find recommendations for China on both of these platforms, but it’s largely made by foreign visitors rather than locals.

If you’re looking for inspiration beyond the same five tourist traps or trends for every place you visit, I’d recommend downloading Rednote.

The app is a little funky to use – people post a lot of “live” pictures for a reason I can’t fathom – but the recommendation algorithm is strong. I didn’t need to spend much time searching beforeRednote started showing me content in the destinations I was visiting that was very much my vibe.

The result: I went to many excellent coffee shops and restaurants I otherwise wouldn’t have known about, and where I didn’t see another non-Chinese person.

Unlike the other apps I’ve listed here, this one is nice to have rather than essential, but I found it invaluable for curating my itinerary.

Do I need a Chinese phone number?

Ordering KFC to my train seat was fun, but did require a Chinese number.Katie Collins/CNET

Many people wonder whether they’ll need a Chinese SIM card and phone number while they’re in the country. In my experience, it’s not essential and you should prioritize using an eSIM above anything else.

But if you have a spare phone you can bring, a Chinese SIM card can be worth it. I went into a China Mobile store where I handed over my passport for registration and within half an hour walked out with a free SIM card with enough data to last me until the length of my trip.

The reason I got a local SIM was that I wanted to test out a couple of things (ordering food on the train and Shenzhen’s drone delivery service) that specifically required a Chinese number. I also used the SIM to tether off on a couple of occasions when I was in more rural areas and I couldn’t get my payment apps to work using my eSIM.

By and large, most visitors won’t need a Chinese number, so don’t worry about trying to get hold of a local SIM card – especially if you’re only in the country for a short period of time.

Editors’ note: Katie Collins’ travel costs for the Honor event were covered by Honor. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.
excerpt:
So, you’re going to China and you need to get your phone in order, but you don’t know where to start. That was me, a month ago.

Now I’ve been there, for a week of work and another week of personal travel in and around Shenzhen. In that time, I got a good grasp on the ecosystem of apps and mini-apps. Enough, at least, to get you started if you’re venturing to China anytime soon.

title: MagSafe Monday: Vinich’s MagSafe wallet leans into a classic look
snippet: I’ve been on a spree of trying out new MagSafe wallets that look more like traditional wallets. Vinich’s MagSafe wallet is the latest one I’ve tried. It comes in 15+ colors, looks like a traditional foldable wallet built to sit on the back of a leather iPhone case without clashing with it. It’s designed to look more like an extension of your iPhone case. more…
fullText:
I’ve been on a spree of trying out new MagSafe wallets that look more like traditional wallets. Vinich’s MagSafe wallet is the latest one I’ve tried. It comes in 15+ colors, looks like a traditional foldable wallet built to sit on the back of a leather iPhone case without clashing with it. It’s designed to look more like an extension of your iPhone case.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Color options

The manufacturer clearly wanted to leave no stone unturned when it came to colors. They have options in black, green, brown, and even purple, all with a broken-in, aged look that goes well with a leather case rather than fighting it. They also have countless other colors as well. Vinich also offers Desert Titanium, which goes well with that color iPhone if you opt for a caseless look.

Wallet sotrage

Vinich lists three card slots and says you can realistically fit three to five cards, depending on their thickness. In day-to-day usage, that’s probably a driver’s license, a card or two, and a work access control card. There’s also room to fold a bill or two behind the cards, which I always appreciate in a wallet this size. I try to always keep $20 or so on me

The card compartment is lined with RFID-blocking material, and the interior is lined with microfiber so your cards aren’t rubbing against fabric all day. The magnets are strong enough here. I’ve had stronger ones, but I’ve also had much weaker ones.

Three things to know before you buy

First, this is synthetic leather, not actual real leather. It’s scratch-resistant with reinforced stitching, and at this price point, that’s exactly what you’d expect, but if you’re pairing it with a real leather case, you should know going in that the materials aren’t going to be an exact match. Vinich recommends conditioning it every three to six months

Second, it can slowly inch into the frame on wide-angle and macro shots. It sits below the camera on most iPhones, but for close-up photography, you’ll want to pull it off to make sure it’s not covering the lens at all

Finally, it does not work as a stand, even though it looks like it should. The flap is intentionally flexible to keep stress off the magnetic ring, so if you want a wallet that props your iPhone up for a call or video, this isn’t it.

Wrap up

Sub $25, the color range alone makes this worth a look if you’ve been running a nice leather case with a wallet that doesn’t match it. Most MagSafe wallets are built to disappear. This one is built to go with something, and it feels/looks more like a traditional wallet you’d even carry standalone as well. I’d love to see an option with Find Me integration in the future as well. 

You can buy the Vinich MagSafe wallet from Amazon or directly from Vinich.

title: iOS 26.7 now available for iPhone, here’s what’s new
snippet: Apple launched its major iOS 27 release today for iPhone. But for anyone not yet ready to install the new software version, Apple has also released a smaller iOS 26.7 update. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
Apple launched its major iOS 27 release today for iPhone. But for anyone not yet ready to install the new software version, Apple has also released a smaller iOS 26.7 update. Here’s what’s new.

iOS 26.7 debuts as security fix update for iPhone users not yet ready to install iOS 27

It’s a big day for Apple software releases. The company just debuted iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS Golden Gate, watchOS 27, and a lot more.

But if you’re not ready to install the latest software yet, Apple has another option for you.

iOS 26.7 is now available for iPhone, a minor update for anyone not yet ready to install iOS 27.

The new release includes “security fixes for your iPhone” per Apple’s official release notes.

It’s become common practice for Apple to ship smaller updates to its current OS version on the same day as major new releases debut.

The company typically presents iPhone users with two options. They can install the major new release, or stay on the current version and get additional security updates and bug fixes.

Today, iOS 26.7 is that second option. It doesn’t contain any new features, but it does ensure your iPhone stays up to date with the latest security patches.

The full list of security fixes has been published here. It’s an extensive list of patches, highlighting the importance of installing the update despite its lack of other improvements.

Are you upgrading to iOS 27 or keeping your iPhone on iOS 26.7 for now? Let us know in the comments.

title: Samsung reportedly considers early ‘Galaxy Z TriFold 2’ release in wake of iPhone Duo
snippet: In the wake of iPhone Duo, Samsung is reportedly considering an early release for a Galaxy Z TriFold sequel. more…
fullText:
In the wake of iPhone Duo, Samsung is reportedly considering an early release for a Galaxy Z TriFold sequel.

The Galaxy Z TriFold delivered a wild new form factor to Samsung’s lineup late last year, but it didn’t stick around for long. The TriFold made its US debut in January for $2,900 and was discontinued barely three months later.

There have been rumors flying around a “Galaxy Z TriFold 2” coming in 2027 alongside another new form factor, a slideable, but it sounds like that might be moved up following Apple’s iPhone Duo reveal. 

Leaker Lanzuk says that Samsung is “considering” an early “Galaxy Z TriFold 2” release, with the slideable also being moved up. An exact timeline is unclear, and it’s likely enough that the 2027 timeline will remain.

	

The post also claims that the TriFold sequel will be “thinner, lighter, and more durable” compared to the first generation, with a goal of having the price be “nearly identical.” While $2,899 is still no small price to pay, it’d be impressive if Samsung were able to keep pricing unchanged given the market forces at play, not to mention rumors that the first TriFold was sold at a loss. 

Would you buy a second-generation TriFold?

title: Googlebook pre-orders start on September 21
snippet: After previously teasing a fall timeframe, Google is set to open pre-orders for Googlebooks on Monday, September 21. more…
fullText:
After previously teasing a fall timeframe, Google is set to open pre-orders for Googlebooks on Monday, September 21.

The email blast to users who signed up for updates on the Android-based platform went out this morning. On September 21 at 9 a.m. ET, you’ll be able to pre-order the first Googlebook devices.

You can expect devices from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, with several leaking in recent weeks. By that date, Google will presumably detail the full operating system, including sharing what the actual name is. In May, we only got a preview.

Today’s teaser highlights the Magic Pointer that allows you to access Gemini immediately. This animation transforms into the light bar that all Googlebooks are expected to feature as their marquee branding element. Google has yet to share what exactly it will do. Compared to Chromebooks, this will be the primary brand on the cover. “Googlebooks” only appears on the left palm rest just below the keyboard. 

	

It’s not clear what the gap between pre-orders and device shipments will be, but launching before the holiday shopping season seems likely.

title: I Pretended to Be on Vacation to Test This Rental-Ready Smart Lock
snippet: Lockly released a new type of smart lock, with a stylish keypad and features made specifically for rentals, vacation homes and Airbnbs. I tried it all.
fullText:
This smart lock is built for rentals in all-new ways. / Tyler Lacoma/CNET		

	

		

									

						Lockly Lyro Lasta					

					

	8.0

	
					

			

	

		

			

				Pros & Cons			

			

			

							

					
						Affordable for its tech and design quality					
				

							

					
						Many access options including fingerprint, included cards, keys, keypad and more					
				

							

					
						Extra-large battery case rated for up to three years					
				

							

					
						Easy to manage access and logs through the app					
				

							

					
						Unique sleep mode if the home is going unused for a while					
				

							

					
						Effective and simple TapCom communication include for vacation renters and similar situations					
				

					

			

							

					
						The rental-focused design may not be suited for every home					
				

							

					
						The deadbolt requires manual turning when locked/unlock, which differs from most smart locks					
				

					

	

		

Many smart locks introduced innovations in 2026. We saw charging solar panels and ultrawideband sensing. But Lockly went the opposite way: The security company has launched a new lock called Lyro, which aims at a unique mix of affordability, battery life and new features made specifically for vacation rentals, short-term renting, landlords and similar situations. I’ve never seen anything quite like it.

To test the Lockly Lyro Lasta ($169), I set it up as if I was the owner, and tried to access it in a variety of ways like I was a newcomer on vacation. It’s interesting what features Lockly has added here, and what the company has done with a lock well under $200 that still has a durable design, fingerprint sensor, RFID tags to give out and more. Here’s what I found.

A design made for durability and battery power

This smart lock comes with everything included, like the rental add-ons.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

The Lyro Lasta is mostly a normal smart lock — except for several very important additions. On the front of the lock I found the fingerprint reader and Lockly’s stylish touchscreen keypad, a design I’ve seen on other Lockly products before and found them very reliable. That outward-facing section is also IP65 weatherproof, so you shouldn’t need to worry much about operation in heavier weather.

The inside housing, however, is extra large because it’s made to hold eight AA batteries, something I’ve never seen in a smart lock before, since most are made for four AAs or fewer. Lockly says the extra battery boost lets the lock last for up to three years without needing replacement. It’ll take me a while to see if that’s true.

Lyro Lasta’s 8 AA batteries can supposedly last for years.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

As with most modern locks, this Lyro model doesn’t need a Wi-Fi hub to go online. Installation and setup proved relatively simple. The lock isn’t especially complex, and components are quite sturdy for the price.

Codes, keys and more access options

This Lyro lock has its pecular features, but they all seem to have a purpose.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

In addition to standard keys, keypad code, phone connection and the included NFC tags, I tested this lock’s fingerprint sensor, which boasts a 0.2-second response time (I don’t know about that, but it was under a second), and the ability to hold 99 fingerprints.

Everything proved responsive with smooth operation, but I did run into yet another unique feature of the Lasta that took me by surprise. Almost every other smart lock I’ve tested automatically unbolts the lock when it’s unlocked by any means. Not so here: This lock unlocks internally, but you still need to manually turn either the inside or outside thumbturns to move the deadbolt.

I’m not sure why Lockly chose this approach, which could be confusing to those with experience in smart locks. It may cut down on wear and tear, and it could help save even more battery life, but it’s important visitors know they’ll need to manually move the lock. Fortunately, the lock also introduces all-new ways to communicate with guests.

			

			

							
		

	

		

			Best Home Security Systems for Renters in 2026: Hassle-Free, No Contracts
		

					

You can equip your rental with personalized security options. My picks can fit nearly anywhere — no screws required.

						

		

Lockly TapCom and other rental-friendly add-ons

Lockly’s TapCom proved an effective communication option for guests.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

The plethora of unlocking options are convenient for anyone, but this Lyro lock also has features that make it well-suited for vacation rentals, visitors, Airbnbs and similar situations. The extra battery life, for example, is particularly handy for homes that may stay vacant for part of the year, or have off-seasons with little activity. But that’s only the start.

The physical RFID tags make it easy to hand off access methods to others without fussing with extra pairs of physical keys, and you can disable them by the app if they aren’t returned. Speaking of the app, it also provides owners with an easy-to-use log of activity, and an unusual sleep mode that saves even more battery life if a residence is going to stay unused for a while.

But the most useful rental feature of them all is the TapCom, the platform Lockly offers to help connect and coordinate renters with owners. It’s not the first Airbnb-friendly platform I’ve seen announced this year, but it is one of the first to market and I like what I see.

To use TapCom, owners scan a QR code on a card-sized NFC plate, then stick the plate by the Lyro lock. When guests show up, they can scan the code with their phones or just tap directly on the card to get started. Owners control different ways for guests to communicate and announce their arrival, as questions, wait for remote unlocking, finalize payment info and so on.

In my tests, TapCom allowed me to enable video calls, audio calls and requests to unlock, and geofencing that only enables communication when a phone is right by the TapCom plate. Connections worked accurately in seconds on both phones used in the conversations. Of course, you will need to give the platform a certain amount of access to your mics, phone number, etc. to make this all work.

While these features sound like a particularly good fit for Airbnbs, I can imagine standard landlords and property management companies, along with tenants, would also appreciate such on-demand communication options.

Final thoughts on the Lyro Lasta

Lockly’s inside housing is larger than some to include all those extra batteries.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Lockly’s Lyro Lasta ($169) does a little of everything with unique new features made just for rentals, vacation homes, Airbnbs and similar situations, at a reasonable price.

The extra-long battery life, multitude of access options and free support for the TapCom communication system for new guests all worked flawlessly in my tests, although I was caught off guard by the need to manually turn the deadbolt after it locked/unlocked internally.

The Lyro Lasta is more of a niche product than many smart locks, but it’s a niche with plentiful opportunities, including owners with specific plans on how to manage their property for newcomers. It will be interesting to see what comes of the Lyro line in the future.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Tyler Lacoma
						

						

							Editor / Home Security and Smart Home						
					

											

								

											Tyler has worked on, lived with and tested all types of smart home and security technology for over a dozen years, explaining the latest features, privacy tricks, and top recommendations.
With degrees in Business Management, Literature and Technical Writing, Tyler takes every opportunity to play with the latest AI technology, push smart devices to their limits and occasionally throw cameras off his roof, all to find the best devices to trust in your life. He always checks with the renters (and pets) in his life to see what smart products can work for everyone, in every living situation. 
Living in beautiful Bend, Oregon gives Tyler plenty of opportunities to test the latest tech in every kind of weather and temperature. But when not at work, he can be found hiking the trails, trying out a new food recipe for his loved ones, keeping up on his favorite reading, or gaming with good friends.

title: Gemini app makes Daily Brief free in the US
snippet: After introducing at I/O 2026 in May, Google is making Daily Brief in the Gemini app available for free in the US. more…
fullText:
After introducing at I/O 2026 in May, Google is making Daily Brief in the Gemini app available for free in the US.

Daily Brief generates a list of your to-dos and priorities every morning. Gemini uses Personal Intelligence to look at your Gmail, Google Calendar, and other Connected Apps, as well as past Gemini chats.

The Daily Brief starts with a “Top of mind” section that shows “timely, actionable items,” such as tasks with upcoming deadlines. “FYI” will show other items that have dates attached. “Looking ahead” is the final section with a focus on long-term goals and “suggested next steps to help you achieve them.”

You can tap on items to “Mark complete” or start a “Chat” with Gemini. There’s also the ability to leave “Helpful” or “Not helpful” feedback.

	

Example use cases include:

For students: Manage class schedules, organize study plans, and track applications.

For entrepreneurs: Surface actionable client emails and update task reminders.

For parents: Manage school communications, track family milestones, and handle household tasks.

For job seekers: Quickly act on recruiter inquiries, prepare for interviews, and monitor application statuses.

As of last Friday, Gemini Daily Brief no longer requires a Google AI subscription in the US. It’s available to personal Google Accounts with Personal Intelligence, Memory, and the Google Workspace integration enabled.

You can access it from the Gemini side panel, with Google also sending a notification every morning. You can disable that alert by going to the account menu and configuring “Notifications.” 

Another way to interact with the digest is through Gemini Live: “What’s my daily brief?”

title: Overwatch Season 5 Will Add a New Kind of Support, Try to Solve 2 Roster Headaches
snippet: This year has already brought massive changes to the Overwatch roster, and next season adds two reworks of longtime problem heroes.
fullText:
Overwatch kicked off its 10th anniversary in February by announcing that it was adding 10 new heroes to the hero shooter this year, more than triple the average additions in previous years. But the roster shake-ups aren’t over. Announced at BlizzCon 2026, the ninth of those 10 heroes joins the roster next month, alongside two existing heroes whose gameplay kits have been significantly reconfigured.

I tried the new hero at BlizzCon and spoke with some Overwatch developers about all three heroes being introduced or reintroduced next month.

Season 5 introduces the new support character, Doctrine — a vampiric villain who empowers teammates and enfeebles opponents. His kit-defining ability is his alternate fire, which allows him to boost his other abilities. When paired with his Infuse ability, Doctrine’s primary fire becomes stronger and pierces enemies, his dash grants free flight and his ability to heal and provide allies a boost to attack speed is also applied to himself. 

His ultimate ability, Deliverance, is perhaps the best embodiment of that vampiric fantasy: It sends out a swarm of bat-like drones that provide overhealth to allies while reducing opponents’ maximum life for several seconds. 

“He seems pretty versatile, but I think there’s going to be a high skill ceiling for him as well, because it’s accuracy-based,” Kenny Hudson, lead hero producer on Overwatch, told me in an interview. He also speculated that Doctrine’s ultimate ability will be an important factor in players’ success, which is generally more true for support heroes than other roles.

Doctrine has a somewhat austere, too-important-for-you demeanor that fits the vampire fantasy while also distinguishing him from heroes in the damage role, Art Director Dion Rogers said. Rogers also noted the character’s posture and use of a staff, rather than a gun, as a weapon as a way to embody a dangerous support character without connoting a different role entirely.

I played a few games of Doctrine at BlizzCon — not enough to learn the ins and outs of the character, but enough to see how he functions in a few different situations. I liked the minigame of deciding which abilities to empower and when. 

Playing against an enemy D.Va, I made sure to keep one charge in reserve for when she inevitably flew in my face, shooting rockets. I toyed with my opponent by luring her away from my team before spending an Infuse charge on my Shrouded Momentum ability to fly back up to high ground while she was still stranded elsewhere.

Sometimes it takes a while before the community figures out how to make new supports work, so I’m looking forward to seeing how Doctrine’s trial weekend goes and what players are able to unlock in these few days of experimentation. 

Doctrine has a long history with Doomfist and will play an important role in the story of Season 5.Blizzard

After years of flirting with it, Sombra officially moves over to the support role

Doctrine isn’t the only new support hero in season 5. Longtime damage hero Sombra is sliding over into the support role, with multiple reworked abilities that allow her to heal her allies. She can now use abilities to heal allies and reduce enemies’ damage output, though she’s keeping her translocator ability and EMP ultimate. 

Sombra has seen more reworks than any other Overwatch hero — five, by my relatively lenient count, before this one. The devs have tried repeatedly to find a way to offer players the gameplay fantasy of an invisible hacker while also trying to knock her off the list of most frustrating heroes to play against. 

This time, they took a bigger swing at the changes, while targeting the usual frustrations.

“The idea was [to] take away the frustration of getting hacked and shot out of anywhere and the friction that comes from being unable to use your abilities,” Hudson said. The rework preserves the character’s stealthy hacker identity while reimagining her abilities in ways that more directly help her team. He and Rogers said the early internal playtests surprised people with how well the role swap seemed to click with the character.

Sombra has a long history of being on the edge of support, including being played by support players in the early days of the professional Overwatch League before the game implemented a role lock. More recently, the Mirrorwatch event, which flipped heroes and villains, gave us a vision of Sombra who could support allies by increasing their attack speed — hey, that sounds familiar — and providing them with overhealth.

She’s also one of my most-played damage heroes, trailing only Ashe in total damage playtime. I like being stealthy in video games, so I’ve enjoyed her sneak-around-and-teleport style of gameplay. But I’m historically more of a support player, which means this move is especially interesting to me. I’m very much in favor of the idea of the role swap, but I haven’t seen quite enough of her latest iteration to judge whether I think it’s an effective repositioning of Overwatch’s poster problem child. 

In particular, I wonder whether she’ll have the healing throughput to function in a wide variety of compositions, or whether one player choosing Sombra will effectively require the other support player to choose a hero with more on-demand healing capabilities. One BlizzCon isn’t enough time to answer that, but I’m hopeful that the rework changes her into a functional support hero and not just someone stuck halfway between a maligned damage hero and useful support.

Players line up to try Doctrine and the Sombra and Roadhog reworks at BlizzCon.

Roadhog loses his hook combo (mostly), gains a trash compactor

Joining Sombra on the rework front is Roadhog, who’s staying in the tank role, but with a new, allegedly more team-focused look. Changes to the pull distance of his chain hook and the mechanics of his gun will effectively remove his ability to instantly combo down most heroes, which Hudson said should be “a lot less frustrating” to play against.

He’s getting a new Trash Compactor ability that allows him to nullify incoming damage and convert it into a burst of damage. Scott Kennedy, a hero designer for Overwatch, said in a group interview that the ability was intended to give Roadhog a way of helping his team instead of being more of a lone wolf tank. 

Removing the burst damage of the hook combo should do a lot to lessen the frustration of playing against a Roadhog, but I’m skeptical about how it affects the other side of the equation: playing with a Roadhog on your team. My worry is that he’ll remain a tank who mostly wants to roam around on his own and hook people from unexpected angles, making the rest of the team vulnerable to pushes from the enemy team if the Roadhog misses his skillshot and has to spend time fleeing prospective danger.

Then again, tanking in Overwatch’s 5v5 era has changed a lot, and most tanks benefit from playing different angles from their teams, maximizing the angles of incoming damage that enemy teams have to worry about. Even Reinhardt, Mr. Big Shield Man himself, can often get more value using that shield to protect himself on a threatening off-angle rather than trying to shield his entire team in a clump. So it’s possible that the rework will ultimately make Roadhog more consistent and less of a feast-or-famine hero, which would be a marked improvement. 

We’ll find out when Doctrine and both reworks launch next month for the start of Season 5.

Editors’ note: Adam Benjamin’s travel costs for BlizzCon were covered by Blizzard Entertainment. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

title: YouTube details NFL Sunday Ticket pricing & availability for 2026 season, including a 50% discount
snippet: YouTube is starting its fourth season as the home of NFL Sunday Ticket and, ahead of Week 1 games, an overview of availability and pricing has been detailed, including a big discount for new customers. more…
fullText:
YouTube is starting its fourth season as the home of NFL Sunday Ticket and, ahead of Week 1 games, an overview of availability and pricing has been detailed, including a big discount for new customers.

For the 2026-2027 season, NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube TV will start at $240/year.

That’s thanks to a big discount YouTube is running, but it’s only available for new subscribers. For those eligible, it’s a discount of up to 50%. For existing customers, the costs are $378/year through YouTube TV (in addition to monthly subscription costs) or $480/year through YouTube Primetime Channels.

You can sign up via YouTube’s Sunday Ticket website.

	

NFL Sunday Ticket packages at YouTube

On a support page and through a thread on Reddit, Google details what games are and are not available through NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube this year, and where you can watch those other games.

It breaks down to:

Thursday Night Football: Not available on YouTube/YouTube TV

Sunday Afternoon Games: Out-of-market via Sunday Ticket, in-market via CBS or Fox on YouTube TV, in-market via Paramount+ or Fox One on YouTube

Sunday Night Football: NBC via YouTube TV, Peacock via YouTube

Monday Night Football: ABC/ESPN via YouTube TV, not available on YouTube

NFL Sunday Ticket also does not include preseason or postseason games, as well as some regular season games such as Thanksgiving Day games.

For Week 1 games being played on September 13, YouTube details what games will be broadcast via CBS and Fox and, as such, are not on Sunday Ticket if you live within the local region. So, as an example: If you live in Buffalo, NY, CBS will be broadcasting the Bills at Texans game, which will not be available via Sunday Ticket, but that game will be on Sunday Ticket if you live in Washington, DC.

title: iPhone Duo vs. Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra: Apple’s and Samsung’s Premium Foldables Compared
snippet: From durability to cameras and battery life, here’s how the premium foldable phones stack up.
fullText:
For months, rumors suggested Apple would name its first foldable the iPhone Ultra. But on Wednesday, the company unveiled its highly anticipated device with a different name: the iPhone Duo.

Skipping the Ultra name feels fitting for a foldable that doesn’t quite offer Apple’s highest-end features. The Duo is still a premium device, but it lacks a telephoto camera and has a slightly more modest battery than the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

In that respect, the iPhone Duo is more comparable to Samsung’s similarly palm-size Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, meanwhile, takes things a step further with Samsung’s top-tier camera and battery specs.

	

			

The Duo is designed to be compact and versatile, allowing you to easily watch horizontal videos in landscape mode and vertical content in portrait. On the other hand, the Z Fold 8 Ultra feels similar to a slab phone when closed, thanks to its slim design and more standard dimensions.  (Meanwhile, the smaller Galaxy Z Fold 8 shares design elements with the iPhone Duo. You can read more about how those phones compare here.)

Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 (left) has a more compact design, while the Z Fold 8 Ultra has a taller build that’s more similar to a slab phone.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

The Duo and Z Fold 8 Ultra share the commonality of a high price tag. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB, while the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra starts at $2,100 for the same storage level.

Preorders for the iPhone Duo kick off Oct. 16 for an Oct. 23 release. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is available now.

Here’s how the two foldable phones compare.

iPhone Duo vs. Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra design and displays

The iPhone Duo has a 5.4-inch cover display.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The key difference between the iPhone Duo and the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is in their designs. 

The iPhone Duo is palm-size with a squat, 5.4-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display. The Z Fold 8 Ultra has a more conventional book-style foldable design, with a taller, 6.5-inch cover screen and a larger 8-inch inner display.

A unique feature of the iPhone Duo is its matte, nano-texture inner display that helps to reduce reflections and minimize the crease. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has an anti-reflective coating that also helps to reduce those distractions, but the Duo’s matte finish does a better job at that.

The iPhone Duo has a 7.6-inch matte inner display that helps to reduce reflections and the crease — though you can still see both under certain lighting conditions.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The Z Fold 8 Ultra stands out for its exceptionally thin build, measuring 4.1mm when open and 8.9mm when closed. The iPhone Duo is also fairly thin, measuring 5.2mm when open and 11.3mm when closed.

The Z Fold 8 Ultra is a little lighter, weighing 215 grams, while the Duo weighs 254 grams. It’s a small difference that’s barely perceptible. 

When multitasking, the Duo can only run up to two apps simultaneously, while the Z Fold 8 Ultra supports multitasking with up to three apps. This is aided by the Ultra’s larger main display that prevents apps from feeling cramped. 

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is the most advanced foldable Samsung currently sells.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Perhaps one of the most impressive features of the Duo is its IP68 rating: it can withstand submersion in up to 6 meters of water for 30 minutes and is dust-resistant. The Z Fold 8 Ultra has a more limiting IP48 rating, meaning it can be submerged in up to 1.5 meters of water for 30 minutes and is protected against solid objects larger than 1mm, but not dust or sand. The Duo’s dust resistance is a rarity in the world of foldables and is shared with Google’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

If you value durability and compactness, the iPhone Duo can be a good fit. If you want a foldable phone that feels more similar to a slab phone when closed and a tablet when open, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is a good pick.

The iPhone Duo has two 48-megapixel rear cameras.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

Because the iPhone Duo is compact, it makes some compromises with the cameras. There’s a 48-megapixel main camera and a 48-megapixel ultrawide camera, but no telephoto lens.  The cover display has a 12-megapixel selfie camera, while an “under-display FaceTime camera” sits on the inside screen.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a triple rear-camera system, which includes a 200-megapixel wide-angle, 50-megapixel ultrawide and 10-megapixel telephoto camera. There’s a 10-megapixel selfie camera on each display. 

The Z Fold 8 Ultra has a triple rear-camera system.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

We’ll have to see how the iPhone Duo performs in our camera tests, but the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra shares rear camera optics with the top-of-the-line Galaxy S26 Ultra (hence the shared moniker), and has performed well in our camera tests. 

iPhone Duo vs. Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra processor and battery life

The iPhone Duo is powered by the same in-house A20 Pro chip as the iPhone 18 Pro models. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip for Galaxy. 

Apple doesn’t share specific battery specs, but says the iPhone Duo will give you up to 31 hours of video playback on the inner display, and 44 hours when using the outer screen. When using both screens equally, the company says you’ll be able to go 24 hours before needing to charge.

Samsung boosted battery capacity on its book-style foldable this year, going from 4,400 mAh on the Z Fold 7 to 5,000 mAh on the Z Fold 8 Ultra. That should easily get you through a day without worrying about where the nearest charger is. 

The iPhone Duo has specialized visual layouts that it switches to automatically when the device is unfolded, folded closed or rotated.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

Apple says the iPhone Duo can charge up to 50% in around 20 minutes with a 60-watt adapter or higher. The Z Fold 8 Ultra supports up to 45-watt wired charging, going from empty to 63% in around 30 minutes in CNET’s testing. 

The Duo has a key advantage when it comes to wireless charging: it supports MagSafe, with Qi2 wireless charging up to 25 watts. Meanwhile, the Z Fold 8 Ultra doesn’t have built-in magnets, but if you use a Qi2-compatible case, you can tap into 20-watt wireless charging.

If you prefer being able to easily attach magnetic accessories without a case, the iPhone Duo has the advantage here. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a long-lasting battery that pulled its weight in our testing.

Which phone should you pick?

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a wider inner display, which offers a little more space for watching videos and multitasking.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Whether you go with the iPhone Duo or the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra ultimately depends on how you plan to use your foldable phone. 

The iPhone Duo is designed to better accommodate both horizontal and vertical content on the inner display, while the compact cover is good for quickly sending texts or checking notifications. If you find yourself viewing swaths of content and want a phone that feels a little different — or are deep in Apple’s ecosystem — the Duo could be the right fit for you.

Meanwhile, the Z Fold 8 Ultra operates as more of a standard-feeling phone when closed, opening to a wide, traditional tablet-like display. If you don’t want to stray too far from the design of slab phones but also want a more expansive screen sometimes, the Z Fold 8 Ultra might be a better pick.

Stay tuned for CNET’s review of the iPhone Duo for more details on the experience. For now, you can read our hands-on with Apple’s new foldable, and check out the spec chart below for more on how the phones compare.
