title: LG Denies Allegations Its Televisions Are Always Recording
snippet: Researchers say that they exploited the microphone and content recognition features of an LG TV to listen to user conversations.
fullText:
LG has denied that its TVs eavesdrop on customers, stating that the sets have voice features disabled by default. This follows claims that its TVs could be used to listen to conversations in real time.

Also read: You’ve Heard About Smart Home Hacking: Here’s How It Works and How Likely It Is

The company said in a blog post on Saturday that features, including automatic content recognition, voice recognition and interest-based advertising, are opt-in and not enabled by default.

“The claims made in the recently published video are not true,” an LG representative said in a statement to CNET. The company said LG TVs process voice data only when the voice button on the remote control is pressed and held or the TV’s “wake word” is uttered by the customer.

“Other than these instances, the TVs do not collect or record ambient conversations,” the statement said.

The company said that if the device doesn’t recognize the wake word, no voice data is transmitted to the server, and that the wake word is detected locally and immediately deleted.

Gaming site GamersNexus reported earlier this month that LG TVs could be hacked by a third party to become listening devices, even if a user disables the onboard microphone.

GamersNexus says it used a man-in-the-middle attack on an LG G5 TV to enable it to listen to audio from a remote computer, and says the TV was able to record audio without the TV being connected to the internet. In a man-in-the-middle attack, the hacker intercepts sensitive data by putting itself in between two other entities, such as a user and a web application.

The 2-hour video, compiled with the help of the Level1Techs site, says that hackers could listen to a USB webcam or an HDMI input even when the physical switch located next to the mic was switched off. It said this alleged vulnerability was possible due to the TV’s Automatic Content Recognition feature, which transmits viewing habits and voice requests back to LG.

“LG TVs are able to be utilized as eavesdropping listening devices, in part because of the advertising functionality that’s built into them. We were able to retrieve plain text transcripts of a voice conversation and inputs from the TV,” the video says.

The video also reports that the researchers were able to see a list of the IP addresses of all the other devices on the network, even if those devices weren’t connected to the TV.

“LG TVs feature the ability to scan for and connect to nearby devices on the same network. This is a standard function commonly provided by smart TVs and smart home devices,” an LG statement said.

The LG TV microphone, like many smart devices, is designed to listen for a wake word or phrase such as “Hi TV” and then perform the requested task. 

Meanwhile, Apple says its new “always listening” Audio Intelligence feature doesn’t let the company access users’ raw audio. 

Almost all TVs and streaming devices use automatic content recognition to target ads to customers based on viewing habits, but users can usually disable this feature in the device’s settings.

It’s worth noting that any smart speaker will record audio for a limited time after hearing its wake word. If you somehow disclose your Social Security number during that time, for instance, it will be recorded and transmitted.

Smart-home attacks are rare, but the researchers recommend removing LG TVs from your network to prevent unauthorized data collection and privacy breaches. Unprotected computers and routers, not televisions, are the most likely targets for hackers.

title: John Ternus and Greg Joswiak reveal why now is the time for iPhone Duo
snippet: Following this week’s Apple event, new Apple CEO John Ternus and marketing SVP Greg Joswiak sat down for an interview to talk more about the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. In the interview with Tom’s Guide and TechRadar, Ternus and Joswiak discussed why Apple decided that now was the time to enter the foldable market. Ternus also touched on his feelings after his first week as Apple CEO. more…
fullText:
Sc			
	

Following this week’s Apple event, new Apple CEO John Ternus and marketing SVP Greg Joswiak sat down for an interview to talk more about the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo.

In the interview with Tom’s Guide and TechRadar, Ternus and Joswiak discussed why Apple decided that now was the time to enter the foldable market. Ternus also touched on his feelings after his first week as Apple CEO.

On why Apple felt now was the time to announce iPhone Duo, Ternus explained:

“I think for us, it’s always about when do we feel like we have a product idea that meets our bar for quality and durability, but also for design. What I think is particularly amazing about the Duo is, it’s such a good example of hardware and software coming together to make something really special.

It was like a green field of opportunity for us because there was opportunity to rethink so many different things. And I think you see that in the hardware, and you see that in the software, and the design. It all kind of came together and felt like it was the right product.

Joz, meanwhile, added that what Apple saw other smartphone makers doing in the foldable space “wasn’t very inspiring.”

“If you’ve seen what’s been out there, not only is it just kind of cheap-feeling plastic surfaces, they don’t feel good to touch, they’re kind of wavy, wrinkly,” Ternus added in reference to the displays of competing foldable phones.

Ternus was also asked about the moment he first found out he was going to be CEO of Apple:

It’s amazing, what an extraordinary privilege, right? The reality is I just, I love this place. It’s in my blood. I’ve been here for half my life. I love the people I work with. I love to be able to build the products that we all build together. And so goosebumps, excitement and yeah, just real, like really, really excited about the future.

title: Someone recreated the iPhone Duo’s mesmerizing open animation on the Galaxy Z Fold 8
snippet: It’s been less than a day since Apple announced the iPhone Duo, and someone has already taken the instantly iconic Apple iPhone Duo unfolding animation and applied it to their Galaxy Z Fold 8. Don’t get too excited, because it isn’t exactly available for everyone. more…
fullText:
It’s been less than a day since Apple announced the iPhone Duo, and someone has already taken the instantly iconic Apple iPhone Duo unfolding animation and applied it to their Galaxy Z Fold 8. Don’t get too excited, because it isn’t exactly available for everyone.

If you caught any of Apple’s iPhone event, you’ll undoubtedly be familiar with the iPhone Duo. Much like Google, Apple is entering the space with a passport-sized foldable phone to appeal to a wider number of users over the taller, slimmer design Samsung pioneered for the last few years. Even Samsung has added the shorter, wider form factor to its lineup.

That’s what makes what one user did for their Galaxy Z Fold 8 such a natural next step after Apple’s announcement. Someone recreated Apple’s iPhone Duo unfolding animation for the Galaxy Z Fold 8. They shared their work on Reddit, and it looks extremely close to what the early hands-on and promo videos show on the new folding iPhone.

The animation on the iPhone Duo creates this sort of blue effect, stuck in perceived space. When you open the phone, apps and home screen content stay locked in space while it looks like your phone physically reorients itself around software. It fits right in line with the liquid glass design philosophy, with app icons coming into focus as the phone opens wider.

	

On the Galaxy Z Fold 8, it can be done by assigning hinge extension values to frames of an animation. In effect, opening the Fold 8 plays an animation at the speed the phone unfolds.

That’s where the downside of this fun little trick lies. Since it’s an animation of two screenshots with a blur effect, it can’t be built into the SystemUI. At least, not in the current state Samsung makes it available.

That doesn’t detract from the sheer hype in the comments. It’s clear that even a GoodLock copycat feature would be welcomed with open arms. If one thing was clear, the iPhone Duo shines in UX design, and competition between Android foldables and now Apple’s might mean Samsung adds more refined features that make the overall experience feel cleaner.

title: KitchenAid’s New Design Series Mixer Has a Glass Bowl That Illuminates
snippet: The Luminaire comes in a new blue peppercorn color and features an entirely redesigned glass bowl.
fullText:
KitchenAid released its newest Design Series stand mixer on Tuesday with a distinctive feature created specifically to pair with the brand’s new built-in LED light: a transparent glass bowl.

The Luminaire debuted in a brand new color, blue peppercorn, but the icy blue shade isn’t the only thing that makes the mixer stand out. The redesigned glass bowl allows the built-in LED light to shine through. The light is a feature KitchenAid introduced earlier this year, and is the true focal point of this launch. 

While this isn’t KitchenAid’s first glass bowl for a mixer, the 3.5- and 5-quart glass options you can purchase separately from the mixer have been due for a redesign. Brittni Pertijs, design manager of color, material and finish at Whirlpool Corporation, KitchenAid’s parent company, said in a statement shared with CNET that the design team hadn’t touched the glass bowl design in nearly a decade, until now. 

	

			

How the Luminaire’s design differs

The Luminaire’s bowl design is entirely different from both the older glass bowl options and its stainless steel counterparts. It features hardened glass for extra durability and a fluted design in a light blue color. Instead of having a single handle on the side of the bowl, the handles were moved to the top, creating more visual appeal. 

“The bowl was a big focus,” Pertijs said. “We wanted it to feel just as functional as it is beautiful. We were inspired by traditional pieces like vintage china, cut crystal and French influences and explored a wide range of how decorative we could go. There were many iterations around the fluting, the depth and how the pattern interacts with the glass, as we worked to find the right balance between decorative and modern.”

The glass bowl idea was partly inspired by KitchenAid’s launch of the Artisan Plus stand mixer, which introduced a precision speed dial, a soft-start feature and a built-in LED light that automatically turns on when the tilt-head is lowered. These features help make the Artisan Plus CNET’s favorite stand mixer.

When testing the Artisan Plus, the light quickly became my favorite new feature, since it seemed like a practical improvement for visibility while using the appliance. But I can see how pairing it with the textured glass bowl can elevate the mixer even further, turning the renowned countertop appliance into a centerpiece in your kitchen, too. 

The Luminaire comes with stainless steel attachments.KitchenAid

Will Luminaire be Evergreen?

This isn’t the first time KitchenAid’s design series has put extra focus on the bowl itself. In 2024, the Evergreen Design Series model featured a walnut wood bowl that quickly went viral on social media.

KitchenAid seemed to launch Evergreen at exactly the right time, when green was one of the most popular paint color options (and the trend is still going strong with paint brand Behr naming Grounded, a mossy green, the 2027 color of the year). But KitchenAid is no rookie at choosing colors that make a statement, and the brand may be onto another big color trend with the Luminaire. 

Paint brands Glidden and Valspar both chose shades of blue for their 2027 Colors of the Year. Let’s wait and see if other brands and consumers follow suit.  

The Luminaire is now available for $700.

title: Apple says two iOS 27 features aren’t coming until a ‘future software update’
snippet: This week, Apple announced that iOS 27 will be released to everyone on Monday, September 14. Along with that, the company now says two features included in the iOS 27 betas have been removed and will be released in a “future software update” for iPhone: suggestions in Messages and automatic password changes. more…
fullText:
This week, Apple announced that iOS 27 will be released to everyone on Monday, September 14.

Along with that, the company now says two features included in the iOS 27 betas have been removed and will be released in a “future software update” for iPhone: suggestions in Messages and automatic password changes.

Apple updated its website this week to reflect that it has pulled these features from iOS 27 for now. The change also applies to other platforms, including iPadOS 27 and macOS 27. Reddit users had noticed that the automatic password change feature was removed in iOS 27 beta 5, and Apple has now updated its website to confirm that change.

As a refresher, suggestions in the Messages app use the context of a user’s conversation to add things to Reminders, Notes, or Calendar with just a single tap.

Here’s how Apple describes the Passwords feature:

“Fix passwords with a tap: The Passwords app alerts you to weak or compromised passwords and can update them on your behalf without the hassle.”

The Passwords app attempts to go directly to websites where your password is weak or compromised and update them automatically. At WWDC, Apple explained that the feature uses Apple Intelligence and Safari to “agentically take action on your behalf.”

There are no additional details on when these two features will return to iOS 27. Apple’s website simply says they are coming in a “future software update.”

title: Apple made fun of Android apps on foldables, but iPhone Duo has the same problem [Gallery]
snippet: Apps have always been a problem for foldable displays and, while they’ve gotten a lot better, there’s always room for improvement. fullText:
Apps have always been a problem for foldable displays and, while they’ve gotten a lot better, there’s always room for improvement. Apple was already going to hold an advantage here, as we’ve previously discussed, but a moment during the iPhone Duo’s unveiling sticks out – Apple made fun of how Android foldables sometimes letterbox apps on the inner display, but it turns out that iOS does exactly the same thing.

In the early moments of the iPhone Duo’s announcement, new Apple CEO John Ternus called out “others” who have already launched foldables, with a background video showing the age-old problem – letterboxed apps.

To quote new Apple CEO John Ternus:

Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones awkwardly stuck together. This results in a square screen that’s poorly suited for the way people use them. Scrolling through vertical content feels compromised, and movies are boxed in by oversized black bars, making a larger screen feel much smaller.

Here’s the clip:

	

This was a pretty major problem in the early days of Android foldables. While Android apps have always been good at scaling, the unique form factors of those early days often found weird middle grounds or, even more frequently, apps just hadn’t been updated to be viewed on anything other than an ordinary smartphone display aspect ratio. At the time, it was a wise move on Google’s part, but the problem has been going away thanks to a push on Google’s part as well as the wider adoption of these form factors. Heck, Android foldables got a tablet layout for Instagram before the iPad did. 

So, while watching today’s event, my reaction to that little dig was that Apple is just finding old problems to make Android look bad, again – not exactly new behavior. 

But then our sister site 9to5Mac dug up Apple’s own documentation of how iOS 27.1 will handle apps on the foldable display and, lo and behold, Apple is doing the same thing.

If an app isn’t updated to support iOS 27, it gets boxed in with black bars on either side, showing a portrait view of the app instead. If it isn’t ready for iOS 27.1, it still can’t take up the display area off to the side where the sidebar is.

This was my actual reaction.

As mentioned, Apple has an app advantage in that iOS developers will likely be much quicker to adopt this new form factor. I’m already jealous of that Slack app Apple briefly showed; Slack, you literally had that on Android half a decade ago, bring it back.

Thoughts?

title: Instagram chief thinks a chronological feed is ‘much worse’ and says the quiet part out loud
snippet: As new legislation in Australia aims to let users opt out of the algorithmic nature of modern social media, Instagram’s Adam Mosseri has said that the experience of a chronological feed is “much worse.” more…
fullText:
As new legislation in Australia aims to let users opt out of the algorithmic nature of modern social media, Instagram’s Adam Mosseri has said that the experience of a chronological feed is “much worse.”

Reported by ABC, Mosseri said that “the average user experience gets much worse” when going back to a chronological feed. The Instagram chief added:

If you go to a chronological feed, it ends up getting overwhelmed with content from companies, brands, and publishers… Creators get drowned out, and then your friends get drowned out even more… You miss a lot more content … and you spend a lot less time on the platform…

That last bit is pretty telling, but there’s certainly a point to be made here.

In a chronological feed versus an algorithmic one, a larger quantity of posts would indeed improve reach and, as such, constantly-online influencers, businesses, and others would absolutely benefit from their ability to post more content. That could drown out content from close friends, assuming the user is actually following all of these other accounts in the first place. 

	

Mosseri says that engagement dropped by as much as 50% when switching back to a chronological feed. While Australia is looking to give users an opt-out from algorithmic feeds, Instagram has already complied with legislation that requires it to give the choice to the user such as in the Netherlands, the report brings out. All users can switch to a chronological feed today, but the app always defaults to the algorithmic feed when it is opened.

title: Apple on wide Android foldables beating iPhone Duo; ‘they got the aspect ratio’
snippet: If it feels like it’s been a quiet week for Android news, it’s not just because Monday was a holiday in the US. As is often the case, pretty much everyone got out of the way of Apple’s latest iPhone announcement, which saw the company launch its first-ever foldable. Joining the party this late is down to lead to some questions towards the company’s leadership, but a new interview with Apple’s fresh-faced CEO helps shine some light on how the brand views its Duo competitors. more…
fullText:
If it feels like it’s been a quiet week for Android news, it’s not just because Monday was a holiday in the US. As is often the case, pretty much everyone got out of the way of Apple’s latest iPhone announcement, which saw the company launch its first-ever foldable. Joining the party this late is down to lead to some questions towards the company’s leadership, but a new interview with Apple’s fresh-faced CEO helps shine some light on how the brand views its Duo competitors.

The folks at Tom’s Guide and TechRadar sat down with Apple CEO John Ternus and SVP of Marketing Greg Joswiak to dish on the iPhone Duo, and the pair had some thoughts for their Android-based competition. Ternus started with a comment on what he sees as “cheap-feeling plastic” surfaces on devices like the Pixel 11 Pro Fold or Galaxy Z Fold 8, praising the Duo’s nanotexture finish as the solution to the typical polymer displays foldables are required to use. Ternus also pointed out that the device was largely kept secret, though that “they” — Samsung and other rivals, presumably — managed to learn about the aspect ratio ahead of time.

Ternus and Joz also commented on the software side of the device, pointing to their relationships with developers as a reason the iPhone Duo will outperform its competitors when the device launches next month. The pair specifically highlighted Slack, Netflix, and Zoom as apps that will be optimized for the foldable come day one, though early adopters should definitely prep themselves for some familiar black borders. Apparently, the month and a half gap between the Duo’s announcement and its launch date is also part of the plan, echoing back to the three-month gap the iPad received in 2010 to give third-parties time to make changes to their apps.

Apple also sees the redesigned iOS experience on the Duo as the smartest way to approach foldable software, calling it “incredibly intuitive” and helping to make the overall experience “continuous. I will say, paired with some truly slick animations when opening the display, Apple’s foldable iPhone could have a leg up on its Android competition in that regard, and I’m fascinated to see how companies like Samsung and Google respond to a company as traditionally conservative in its design doing something as massive as moving the dock. Those answers, I would think, will likely arrive throughout 2027.

	

The entire interview, embedded above, is worth a watch, even if I assume most of the people reading this article likely aren’t interested in switching to the iPhone Duo. Ternus and Joz also tackle the stylus question — in their eyes, Jobs’ famous quote about using a stylus with a smartphone doesn’t apply here — and claim they see the Duo as “a great value.” Plus, it’s a chance to get better acquainted with Apple’s new CEO outside of following orders in renaming Lake Ontario in Apple Maps, just as the Sundar Pichai-led Google did last month.

title: iPhone Duo hands-on videos reveal Android foldable pain points we know too well
snippet: Apple has a track record of waiting until the kinks get worked out before it tries its own hand at new devices, but hands-on videos of the iPhone Duo are already starting to show that Apple suffers from some of the same pain points other manufacturers like Samsung do, like the beloved screen crease. more…
fullText:
via Brian Tong			
	

Apple has a track record of waiting until the kinks get worked out before it tries its own hand at new devices, but hands-on videos of the iPhone Duo are already starting to show that Apple suffers from some of the same pain points other manufacturers like Samsung do, like the beloved screen crease.

Samsung has faced some backlash over the years as its continued to develop the Galaxy Z Fold line, as it rightfully should. Flaws exist on these $1,800+ phones, like an ever-present visible crease down the hinge line on the inner display or a less-than-invisible under-display camera.

It turns out Apple hasn’t been entirely successful at perfecting those flaws in its own design. Early hands-on videos are already starting to go live after Apple’s event in Cupertino, and more are very much on the way. Videos like this one from Brian Tong show some interesting details Apple’s keynote left out.

For one, the iPhone Duo’s inner screen is anti-reflective, but it comes off as matte more than anything. It’s a massive contrast from the outer display, which is made from Ceramic Shield 2. Sitting in stark contrast to that matte inner display is the under-display camera, which Apple showed off several times during its keynote. It’s something Samsung dropped from the Galaxy Z Fold design when it launched the latest models, for one reason or another.

	

The iPhone Duo’s under-display camera has no matte finish. That change in finish only serves to highlight a camera that’s supposed to be hidden from view.

Of course, it was never going to be completely hidden, and Apple’s pre-release footage and renders rightfully showed off a camera that was clearly hiding under an area of fewer pixels. Samsung used the same approach in the Galaxy Z Fold 6, but it’s always been just as noticeable. In reality, the camera seems far more noticeable because of the differing reflectivity.

Beyond that, we get a good look at the iPhone Duo’s inner screen crease. It was expected Apple would refine its foldable’s inner display design so a crease would be far less visible than current Android options, but the crease looks just as visible as it does on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra. Apple is using a two-layer flexible glass, which helps prevent a buildup in tension that would cause materials to bind up in the middle.

Still, the crease is a factual aspect of the iPhone Duo. That isn’t to say Apple hasn’t done a good job of hiding it, but it’s an unfortunate aspect of foldable phones for the time being.

The new foldable’s specs also reveal its IP68 water and dust resistant rating is also expected to be temporary, similar to the Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold.

If Apple excels anywhere with the iPhone Duo its in how it designed iOS 27 around the new phone. Compared to where Android and One UI are in their respective builds, Apple’s approach feels much more purposeful for a phone that forces you to look at it a different way. It’s only a matter of time before Android manufacturers begin to copy some of these UX design choices. It introduces welcome competition.

title: Apple Could Be Working on Multiple Foldable Phones, Report Predicts
snippet: Apple just opened the door to foldable iPhones, and the Duo may not be alone for long.
fullText:
Apple could be planning a family of foldable phones in the next few years, building on its newly announced iPhone Duo, according to one tipster.

Trusted Apple leaker Mark Gurman of Bloomberg predicts that Apple will eventually sell more than the basic foldable iPhone Duo. In fact, he says Apple may have chosen the three-letter name Duo — similar to Air and Pro — because a short name “leaves room for a suffix” such as Max or Mini.

“It’s easy to foresee Apple launching an iPhone Duo Max with a larger display, or perhaps an iPhone Duo SE or iPhone Duo mini as either a stripped-down version or a clamshell model,” he writes.

Gurman, who wrote about the iPhone Duo in March 2026, predicts in his latest Power On newsletter that “foldables will make up the majority of new phone sales” in the next decade. He suggests that the iPhone Duo will become the predominant foldable phone on the market next year.

The biggest issue with such predictions is that they depend entirely on consumer demand, which is tough to foresee. Recently, Apple was rumored to be working on a cheaper version of its Apple Vision Pro AR headset, but it is said to have pivoted to smart glasses instead. And analyst Gene Munster long predicted the release of an Apple HDTV, but now says, “just because Apple is working on a product doesn’t mean it will see the light of day.”

Yet, Gurman says that the iPhone Duo, which can be preordered beginning Oct. 16 ahead of an Oct. 23 release, “has gotten it right from day one.” At $2,000 and up, though, the iPhone Duo costs around twice as much as most single-screen flagship phones, and is unlikely to replace them any time soon.

The Apple iPhone Duo was announced last week, but the company’s first foldable phone still trails competitors by many years. Samsung’s Galaxy Fold was released in 2019, before the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Sources say Automattic’s board is out after failed attempt to oust CEO Matt Mullenweg
snippet: Given that these departed board members were those who voted to put Mullenweg on a paid leave of absence to begin with, it makes sense that a board shakeup has taken place.
fullText:
Automattic’s board is out, multiple sources have confirmed to TechCrunch, after last week’s attempt to oust CEO Matt Mullenweg by voting to put him on a paid leave of absence. 

After the vote, Mullenweg, the WordPress founder and CEO of WordPress.com parent company Automattic, accused the board of conspiring against him in a post on Automattic’s Slack. On Friday, TechCrunch exclusively reported that Mullenweg told the company’s staff that he was back in control of the company, also via Slack post. Automattic confirmed to TechCrunch on Saturday that he had returned.

Initially, we heard from sources that Toni Schneider, a founding CEO at Automattic who now leads the open social network Bluesky, had resigned his Automattic board seat. Schneider has since removed a paragraph from his bio page on his personal website that had noted his contributions at Automattic.

Previously, Schneider’s website read: “I also contribute actively at Automattic, the open source company behind WordPress.com and WooCommerce. I was Automattic’s founding CEO and continue to support internal projects and investments as a board member and special advisor.”

We’ve also heard that Mullenweg removed the two other board members, Sue Decker and Gen. Ann Dunwoody. (We later confirmed that Mullenweg removed Dunwoody, but Decker resigned). 

Decker’s LinkedIn bio has been updated to confirm that she served on Automattic’s board from March 2020 through September 2026, despite her name still appearing on Automattic’s Board of Directors page at the time of publication.

Image Credits:LinkedIn screenshot

When asked by TechCrunch about the board changes, Automattic declined to provide specifics, but offered a statement acknowledging that people have left.

Via an email that arrived after midnight PT on Sunday, an Automattic spokesperson shared the following:

“Matt and Automattic’s leadership team have great respect for everyone involved. While we can’t comment on specific individuals, we’re thankful for their contributions to Automattic and its mission, and we remain excited about what’s ahead with Matt at the helm. Matt was away for only 33 hours and 20 minutes—we’re now back to work,” the spokesperson said.

Given that these departed board members were those who voted to put Mullenweg on a paid leave of absence to begin with, it makes sense that a board shakeup has taken place. It also explains how Mullenweg’s return to his position as CEO would have the “full support of the board,” as a statement issued on Saturday indicated. 

TechCrunch is hearing from sources that Automattic may make an internal announcement about the new board sometime on Monday.

In addition to the board departures, Automattic’s Chief Legal Officer Andy Missan also updated his LinkedIn bio, showing he’s no longer at the company as of September 2026. We understand Mullenweg let him go, along with CFO Mark Davies, who was to be the interim CEO.

What prompted the board’s vote still remains unclear. Mullenweg and Automattic are involved in a high-profile lawsuit with a WordPress hosting company, WP Engine. Mullenweg has accused the company of infringing on the WordPress trademark and not sufficiently contributing in terms of engineering hours or money to the open source WordPress effort. Earlier this year, WP Engine claimed in a court filing that Automattic planned to target other competitors with royalty fees. 

More recently, it has accused Mullenweg of allegedly destroying evidence related to the case in apps like WhatsApp, Signal, and Telegram. Last year, Mullenweg had deactivated the accounts of several WordPress contributors over alleged plans to fork the open source software.

title: Before You Get That Phone Deal, Double-Check Bill Credits and Installment Plan Details
snippet: Wireless providers might have amazing deals that give you a brand-new $1,000 phone for free. But make sure to understand the pros and cons before accepting one.
fullText:
With phone prices climbing higher than ever, it’s no wonder most people turn to carrier financing to buy a new phone. Not only can you spread out your payments over time, but cellular companies often offer enticing deals to win customers over, especially if you’re switching to a new provider. Depending on the deal, sometimes you can even get your new phone for free. 

But those deals can be a little confusing, and involve caveats and rules that aren’t always clear. Very rarely is a discount given without a catch. You might also come across terms like “bill credits” or “trade-in credits” that you don’t fully understand.

If you want to know what these terms mean or other details, like what happens if you decide to switch carriers midplan, read on as we walk you through what you need to know before accepting a new carrier deal. 

This article was made possible in part by T-Mobile. It was written and edited independently without partner oversight.

What is carrier financing?

Wireless providers often have financing deals for new phones, versus paying for a new device upfront.Sarah Tew/CNET

Simply put, instead of paying up front for a new phone, carrier financing lets you pay for the phone over time through an installment plan. So, for example, if a phone is $1,200, you can spread the cost over 24 months, which translates to just $50 a month. That’s a lot easier for most people to manage. 

It’s worth noting that you will still need to pay upfront costs, like activation fees and taxes on the new phone, whether you’re on an installment plan or not. Sometimes carriers do offer deals that let you spread that out over time. T-Mobile, for example, has the Equipment Installation Plan Flex 36 that will spread out the payment of the device, fees and taxes over 36 months, making the initial cost zero. That said, you still need to qualify for the plan, and depending on your credit, you could have to pay interest on top of that. 

One particular downside of carrier financing is that it locks you into that carrier for an extended period (usually two to three years). This means you can’t use your phone with another carrier during this time. If you want to end your agreement with the carrier, that will usually result in early termination fees, or ETFs. 

Being stuck with a carrier-locked phone is sometimes bad news if you travel a lot and want to use international eSIMs, which only work with unlocked phones. Otherwise, you’ll have to use your carrier’s international data plan, which can be more expensive. 

What are trade-ins and bill credits?

It might be time to trade in that old iPhone and get bill credits toward the cost of a new one.James Martin/CNET

When shopping around for new phones, you might see the words “bill credit” or “trade-in credit” advertised by a carrier. For example, a carrier might offer a trade-in credit of up to $1,000 if you trade in your existing iPhone for a new one. Then they might say that the trade-in credit will be paid to you as 24- or 36-month bill credits. 

What does all of that mean? First, let’s talk about that trade-in credit. Not all phones will be eligible for one. Often, the carrier will only give a trade-in credit for newer phones. The newer the device, the more trade-in credit you will get. So that out-of-date iPhone 11, for example, probably won’t be worth very much, if at all. 

It’s also worth looking into what else is required for you to get that trade-in credit. Sometimes carriers will only offer the trade-in credit if you sign up for a more expensive monthly plan with services you might not need. Other times, however, the carrier just wants you to switch over, so you might not need to do that. 

Let’s say you agree to the terms and the carrier offers you that $1,000 trade-in credit. Here’s where bill credits come in. If the carrier says the trade-in credit will be paid over 36 months of bill credits, it means that $1,000 will be paid off over the period of 36 months. You won’t get a lump sum of that $1,000 credit instantly, and the credits you do get can’t be cashed out and can only be used toward the amount of your phone bill.

But let’s say you don’t have a phone to trade in at all. You could still save some money if you don’t mind switching carriers. Sometimes carriers will offer to pay for your device as an incentive to switch over to their company. Again, device payments are often applied as bill credits spread over a 24- or 36-month period. 

What happens if I pay off my plan early?

The iPhone Duo is Apple’s most innovative and expensive phone.Patrick Holland/CNET

You can certainly pay off the remaining balance on your phone if you don’t mind paying the upfront cost. However, be warned that you’ll also forfeit any remaining credits you received for the device you traded in. You could also forfeit any other discounts that you agreed to upon signing up for the plan. Be sure to read through the early payoff rules before deciding to pay off your phone ahead of schedule. 

What if I want to switch carriers?

Switching wireless providers can have its advantages, but consider the cost, especially if you haven’t completed any device installment plans that you have.AT&T/Verizon/T-Mobile/CNET

If you want to switch carriers while you’re in an existing installment plan, you might have to pay ETFs to end your current agreement. However, most major carriers like T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon will offer carrier-switching incentives where they’ll pay your ETFs for you. Bear in mind that there’s often a cap on how much of the ETF they will cover. The payment is also often in the form of bill credits. 

You can take advantage of carrier deals when choosing this route. T-Mobile, for example, has a five-year price guarantee that locks in the price of text, talk and data for at least five years. AT&T is also attempting to draw new customers with a modular Build-A-Plan that lets you customize your plan according to your budget. Verizon recently introduced Simplicity, an unlimited phone plan that usually costs $45 a month, but is just $30 a month for new customers who bring their own number.

snippet: Apple is giving the Apple TV Remote app experience a lot of love in iOS 27. That’s as good a sign as any that a new Apple TV 4K box is on the way. more…
fullText:

Apple TV Remote is about to get a lot more useful.

2. Top Shelf content from the selected app on your Apple TV, with… pic.twitter.com/aOFoToCnrR

title: It took way too long for someone to make USB-C cables that say what they can actually do [Gallery]
snippet: Life with USB-C is great, except for the one nagging problem that’s been there since the beginning – you never really know what you’re getting. While it’s not quite the “Wild West” anymore, I was thrilled to see that someone finally made a collection of USB-C cables that not only do what they say they’ll do, but literally have their specs printed on the cable itself. more…
fullText:
Life with USB-C is great, except for the one nagging problem that’s been there since the beginning – you never really know what you’re getting. While it’s not quite the “Wild West” anymore, I was thrilled to see that someone finally made a collection of USB-C cables that not only do what they say they’ll do, but literally have their specs printed on the cable itself.

USB-C is probably one of the most underrated things to happen in mobile tech, maybe ever? Even 10 years ago it was still hard to imagine being able to use the same cable type across your phone, tablet, laptop, or anything else, but that’s very much the reality of today. In theory, one could go on a trip with just a single USB-C cable and be able to charge up their laptop, smartphone, tablet, gaming handheld, headphones, and a number of other pieces of tech with just that one cable. There are still dedicated cables for some things, like smartwatches, but the “Universal” part of USB finally feels true.

The problem is just that it’s really hard to buy the right cable.

It’s not hard to find a USB-C cable – they’re literally everywhere. But the one problem with this standard is that it’s so flexible that two different cables can serve wildly different tasks. A basic cable might be able to charge up a phone at around 20W, but not be able to transfer data at all.. Meanwhile, another cable on the higher end might support 12x the power while also being capable of display output and 40GBps of data transfer. Yet, at a glance, they probably look essentially identical. Even if you bought the right cable for a specific application – let’s say charging a laptop at 100W – you might not be able to tell it apart from the dozen others in your bag.

	

I’ve been frustrated by this problem countless times over the years, and equally annoyed that there wasn’t a good solution to finding the “right” cable besides just ordering a new one. So I’m glad to see that someone has finally fixed this – though I’d never have guessed it’d be a YouTube channel’s merch shop.

LTTStore launched “TrueSpec” cables early this year with the promise of not only strictly adhering to USB-C spec on the cables it sells, but also clearly messaging what the cable can do on both the packaging and the cable itself. It took way too long for someone to do this consistently. There have been cables here or there with labels, but it’s been rare and usually with some negative factor, like inconsistent labeling or a small lineup.

“TrueSpec” hits what I’ve wanted. Each cable has a label etched into either end, quickly identifying what power and data transfer speeds the cable is capable of. The cables themselves aren’t anything fancy beyond this label, but the build quality is obvious with some thick rubber sheathing. Admittedly, I do wish the cable was thinner – it’s pretty bulky and heavy, which is a little annoying in a backpack – but the pros outweigh the cons in my book. 

They’re also admittedly not cheap at all. USB C-C cables start at around $22 and A-C at around $17. 

LTT TrueSpec USB C-C cables

LTT TrueSpec USB A-C cables

	

It’s not like this is some completely unprecedented idea. 

Labels on USB-C cables have been done before, and there are options out there with labels on the cable ends just like this – the organization behind USB-C even has documentation on how to implement this for crying out loud. It’s just so uncommon that “TrueSpec” is easily the most polished and clear effort to actually deliver on this idea. 

LTTStore also sent out some of their other products – this article isn’t sponsored in any way, to be clear – including the infamous LTT Screwdriver and Precision Kit, and I’ve enjoyed using them both. The Screwdriver in, well, screwdriver tasks, and the Precision Kit has been a great add-on to my recent endeavor to clean out my closet of old “spicy pillow” smartphone batteries by removing those batteries from the phone for easier disposal – more on that in a coming 9to5Google Weekender edition.

title: Four ways to achieve shallow depth of field without buying the iPhone 18 Pro
snippet: The variable aperture lens of the shiny new iPhone 18 Pro goes almost one stop wider than the fixed aperture lens in its predecessor: up from f/1.78 in the iPhone 17 Pro to f/1.48 (a smaller number is wider). In principle, this will allow for slightly shallower depth of field, enabling greater separation between your subject and the background – although it’s a relatively small difference. But there are four ways to achieve shallow depth of field (DOF) with much older iPhones … more…
fullText:
The variable aperture lens of the shiny new iPhone 18 Pro goes almost one stop wider than the fixed aperture lens in its predecessor: up from f/1.78 in the iPhone 17 Pro to f/1.48 (a smaller number is wider).

In principle, this will allow for slightly shallower depth of field, enabling greater separation between your subject and the background – although it’s a relatively small difference. But there are four ways to achieve shallow depth of field (DOF) with much older iPhones …

Portrait mode

The most obvious method is, of course, to use Portrait mode, which is specifically designed to allow people to be very clearly separated from the background. 

This is a completely artificial effect using computational photography (assisted by LiDAR, on models that support it) to identify the subject and to apply an artificial blur to everything else. Early versions were extremely crude, but it’s become remarkably good in the last few years.

Macro shots

The second approach is Macro mode, which will be automatically enabled when you get extremely close to something. With this engaged, the iPhone selects the wide-angle camera, which can focus at extremely close distances. 

In this mode, only a few centimetres will be in focus, with everything beyond it increasingly blurred. As you might notice from the example below, you should be prepared to spend a lot of time dusting and cleaning before attempting to photograph anything using this mode! You’ll know the mode is active when you see the yellow flower symbol in the bottom right of the display.

Getting close to the subject

You can also achieve a similar result with the standard camera by getting very close to the subject. For example:

Just tap on the object or person you want to be in focus before taking the photo.

Telephoto shots

A final factor affecting DOF is focal length. All else being equal, the longer the focal length, the shallower the depth of field, and so using the telephoto lens on an iPhone can allow us to achieve a somewhat blurred background.

Combining three methods

Combining three methods works best: 

Select the telephoto lens

Get your subject as far away from the background as possible

Get as close as possible to your subject

This is the best approach to take when photographing people, and is especially effective with the iPhone 15 Pro and later due to the longer focal lengths.

Wrap-up

The wider and variable aperture lens is only one of the new camera features of the iPhone 18 Pro, so you may still want to upgrade if photography is a key application of your phone. But if background blur is your goal, there are other ways to achieve the same thing.

title: Hands-on: Honor’s Robot Phone is probably the coolest phone you still can’t buy
snippet: Decked out with a gimbal and shockingly good camera, the Robot Phone is one of the weirdest devices to come out of Honor. Even if you ignore the fact that it’s limited to China, Honor can’t keep up with demand. more…
fullText:
Decked out with a gimbal and shockingly good camera, the Robot Phone is one of the weirdest devices to come out of Honor. Even if you ignore the fact that it’s limited to China, Honor can’t keep up with demand.

When Honor began teasing a device that hid a fully functional gimbal and a 200MP camera tucked away in its camera bar, it truly seemed like an AI-driven fever dream of what future phones might look like.

Having played around with one this past week, I’m not distancing myself from that thought. Still, I can’t deny it’s a ridiculously cool idea, and a now fully functional Android phone the company launched last month.

Honor’s Robot Phone is aimed at creators more than anyone, for obvious reasons. The 200MP camera sits inside the device’s camera bar, which shouldn’t get you any weird looks if you use it in its retracted form. But as soon as you hit a certain dedicated camera app button and move the physical protective cover, that massive camera rises out of the Robot Phone’s rear panel as if it belonged in a horror movie.

	

The additional 50MP ultrawide and 200MP periscope camera do not move.

The camera app leaves controls up to the user, with full pan/tilt controls and a wide range to cover just about anything in view. It can be flipped 180 degrees for selfie capture, or used outward to record or capture the world in front of you.

Beyond that, Honor has packed some really cool film tools and recording formats. There are panning options and automatic spin controls to get neat shots you’d need to be really skilled to get with your regular old phone. The phone, being a product of Honor’s focus on AI, has object and person tracking. It works better than I anticipated during my short time with the phone, and stabilization was shockingly good for what is, again, a gimbal attached to a phone.

Its bag of tricks is huge, and it was a ton of fun to play around with. Honor pushes a little beyond simple camera tools with the AI-assisted mode, which is what some of the earliest teasers for the phone showcased. MagicOS has an AI assistant named “YOYO,” and it charges it with the ability to look around and gather digital information like a pair of smart glasses would.

It has its struggles when asking it questions in English instead of Chinese, but it’s a neat concept if a little unsettling.

Beyond the camera tools and mechanical gimbal, the Robot Phone brings many of the standard feature sets MagicOS 10 builds out for the manufacturer’s other devices. Overall, it’s a fun and interesting concept that deserves a ton of credit in what can often be a monotonous phone landscape.

At RMB 9,999 – nearly $1,500 – Honor’s Robot Phone is priced well, all things considered. That’s the running price for the 12/512GB configuration. The 16GB/1TB model nears $2,000.

But you probably couldn’t buy it if you wanted to. On top of being launched for the Chinese market with no global launch expected, Honor shared that the device reached sales targets almost immediately. It seemingly kept expectations low, and now has to catch up with demand while supplies are difficult to get a hand on for reasonable prices.

Again, I only messed around with the Robot Phone for a short time, but it ended up being one of those hands-on sessions that reminded me phones can be exceptionally fun. I’m not saying every phone should have an extending gimbal and overkill camera setup, but it’s kind of cool that the option exists – even if heavily limited.

title: Honor Magic 9 Pro Max melds a classic ARRI camera with an iPhone-like look, launches this month
snippet: Honor has officially shown off its next flagship, the Honor Magic 9 Pro Max, which has a pretty familiar-looking design, a massive camera powered by ARRI, and a release date that’s mere weeks away. more…
fullText:
Honor has officially shown off its next flagship, the Honor Magic 9 Pro Max, which has a pretty familiar-looking design, a massive camera powered by ARRI, and a release date that’s mere weeks away.

Honor Magic 9 Pro Max is a new entry to the company’s flagship lineup, arriving on top of the Pro that was at the top of the list in prior years – “Pro Max” is a whole trend this year, it seems.

There’s still a ton we don’t know about this new device, but it’s clear that the camera is right at the center of the conversation.

A huge camera lens on the back takes up over half of the phone’s width, with two other cameras flanking it. They all sit on an iPhone-like camera island with an accent color on the bottom half of the device – this is a very obvious case of “inspiration” drawn from Apple’s latest, though Honor argues the arrangement “draws inspiration from the design language of one of ARRI’s most iconic cinema cameras.” 

	

Honor explains:

The design journey of the HONOR Magic9 Pro Max began with a simple question: How can a device inspire the same sense of creative possibility as cinema? For nearly a century, ARRI has helped filmmakers turn imagination into moving images. In 1937, the iconic ARRIFLEX cinema camera revolutionized professional filmmaking with its legendary “three-lens turret”—a design that brought function, precision, and industrial beauty into one form. Today, HONOR joins hands with ARRI to bring that timeless inspiration to the HONOR Magic9 Pro Max through an all-new camera architecture. (Image attached)

There’s clear inspiration in the camera design, but the phone as a whole certainly brings in some iPhone vibes, and it’s a wild change of pace from last year’s Honor Magic 8.

Specs on the cameras and the phone as a whole aren’t official yet, but ARRI is a part of the processing pipeline, just like on Honor’s Robot Phone. 

Hands-on: Honor’s Robot Phone is probably the coolest phone you still can’t buy

The signature color here is “Moss Green” and Honor says it will fully unveil the Magic 9 Pro Max on September 28. That’s only in China, though, with a global release presumably following later on.

fullText:
Apple TV has a strong fall lineup coming up, including four weeks straight of big premieres that kick off next week with critical hit Slow Horses. Here’s what’s coming.

September 16: Slow Horses (season 6)

Slow Horses continues its streak of debuting new seasons every year, and season 6 sounds like a standout winner per reviews.

This British espionage series based on Mick Herron’s novels returns with more dark humor, thrilling plot twists, and the beloved Slough House crew led by Gary Oldman’s Jackson Lamb.

Here’s Apple’s official series summary:

This darkly funny espionage drama follows a team of British intelligence agents who serve in a dumping ground department of MI5 due to their career-ending mistakes. Led by their brilliant but irascible leader, the notorious Jackson Lamb (Academy Award winner Sir Gary Oldman), they navigate the espionage world’s smoke and mirrors to defend England from sinister forces.

You can watch Slow Horses here on Apple TV.

September 23: Brothers

Brothers pairs stars and longtime friends Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson in a new comedy series with a fun premise.

The showrunner, Lee Eisenberg, is best known as writer and producer behind some of the best seasons of sitcom The Office.

Here’s the official series summary:

“Brothers” follows McConaughey and Harrelson, who play fictionalized versions of themselves, and whose lifelong friendship is thrown into chaos when they uncover a decades-old secret: they might actually be brothers. After Woody’s daughter’s wedding falls apart, he loads up the family and heads to Austin for an extended stay at Matthew’s ranch. But what begins as a healing getaway quickly spirals when Matthew’s mother, Ma Mac (played by Holland Taylor), accidentally lets slip a long-buried secret that the two friends might actually be brothers. As Woody turns the ranch upside down in pursuit of the truth, Matthew finds himself juggling an entirely different identity crisis: a potential run for Governor of Texas. The result is a heartfelt, chaotic and wildly funny story about friendship, family, fame and the messy line between myth and reality.

You can add Brothers to your Apple TV Watchlist here.

October 2: The Last First: Winter K2

The Last First: Winter K2 is a documentary exploring the high-risk practice of extreme mountain climbing.

The film has a 100% Rotten Tomatoes score, and many reviews highlight that it offers a unique angle that could surprise viewers. Per Variety: “The Last First is a revealing look at how they risked their lives for an ideal, maybe for an addiction. It’s a movie that shows us the dark side of literally getting high.”

Here is Apple’s official summary:

In “The Last First: Winter K2,” Amir Bar-Lev tells a complex, harrowing and moving story that takes an unflinching look at the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture. Focusing on a 2021 expedition, this documentary follows Icelander John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara, a party of mountaineers who set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. The men soon find themselves sharing the treacherous ascent with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and a Nepalese team no longer content to help Westerners achieve mountaineering glory. “The Last First: Winter K2” takes us to the icy heights and unpredictable weather of K2 and reveals a surprising and layered story — one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power — all under life-and-death circumstances.

You can add The Last First: Winter K2 to your Apple TV Watchlist here.

October 7 & 9: Small Prophets and Matchbox The Movie

Small Prophets arrives October 7 as a unique addition to Apple TV’s library. Unlike nearly every other show Apple offers for streaming, it’s not original to the service. Instead, Apple licensed the show after it became a hit in the UK earlier this year. It’s an award-winning comedy that viewers around the globe will soon get to enjoy for the first time.

Matchbox The Movie premieres October 9, a new action-comedy film inspired by the Mattel toys. It’s the kind of movie that feels very theatrical, with big stars and a big budget, but will premiere exclusively on Apple TV.

Here are Apple’s summaries for Small Prophets and Matchbox The Movie:

“Small Prophets” is a comic tale of the eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley) who, since his darling Clea disappeared seven years ago, has lived a very ordinary life. He works in a DIY store, visits his dad Brian (Sir Michael Palin) and hopes for Clea to return. One day Brian shares an old recipe involving rainwater, horse manure and more than a little alchemy. With recipe in hand, Michael sets out (albeit with some skepticism) to create homunculi — magical spirits that can predict the future — in the hope they have the answer to his burning question: “will I ever see Clea again?”

“Matchbox The Movie” is an action-packed, globetrotting adventure about a group of friends since childhood who have their lives upended when undercover CIA agent Sean (John Cena), their long-absent former leader, returns to their small town and unwittingly gets them embroiled in a frantic international pursuit to save the world.

Add to your Apple TV Watchlist: Small Prophets and Matchbox The Movie.

title: Today’s NYT Strands Hints, Answers and Help for Sept. 13, #924
snippet: Here are hints and the answers for today’s NYT Strands puzzle, No. 924 for Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026.
fullText:
Looking for the most recent NYT Strands puzzle answers? CNET publishes daily answers and hints for The New York Times Mini Crossword, Connections, Connections: Sports Edition and Strands puzzles.

Strands is like a word find game, but without the list of words to find. Sometimes I see the theme and begin recognizing the answers right away. But for those times when I can’t seem to manage this, there’s a loophole: Strands lets you make as many words of four or more letters as you want. For every three of those words you find, the puzzle will highlight one of the answers. You’re still going to have to unscramble that answer, though, which can be very tough.

I go into depth about the rules for Strands in this story. 

James Bond fans, this puzzle might be one for you. You’ll recognize the theme as the words start to fill in. Read on for hints and all the answers.

Hint for today’s Strands puzzle

Today’s Strands theme is: Top secret.

If that doesn’t help you, here’s a clue: 007.

Clue words to unlock in-game hints

Your goal is to find hidden words that fit the puzzle’s theme. If you’re stuck, find any words you can. Every time you find three words of four letters or more, Strands will reveal one of the theme words. These are the words I used to get those hints, but any words of four or more letters that you find will work:

COUNT, COUNTER, PURE, GREY, TANG, GNAT, RATE, SOLE, RATER, STEER, CRED, CREDIT, RECOUNT

These are the answers that tie into the theme. The goal of the puzzle is to find them all, including the “spangram,” a theme word that reaches from one side of the puzzle to the other. When you have all of them (I originally thought there were always eight, but learned that the number can vary), every letter on the board will be used. Here are the nonspangram answers:

MOLE, AGENT, ASSET, PLANT, OPERATIVE, COUNTERSPY

Today’s Strands spangram

NYT/Screenshot by CNET

Today’s Strands spangram is UNDERCOVER. To find it, start with the U that’s four letters down on the far-left row, and wind down and then across.

Toughest Strands puzzles

Here are some of the Strands topics I’ve found to be the toughest.

#1: Dated slang. Maybe you didn’t even use this lingo when it was cool. Toughest word: PHAT.

#2: Thar she blows! I guess marine biologists might ace this one. Toughest word: BALEEN or RIGHT. 

#3: Off the hook. Again, it helps to know a lot about sea creatures. Sorry, Charlie. Toughest word: BIGEYE or SKIPJACK.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Gael Cooper
						

						

											

								

											CNET editor Gael Fashingbauer Cooper, a journalist and pop-culture junkie, is co-author of "Whatever Happened to Pudding Pops? The Lost Toys, Tastes and Trends of the '70s and '80s," as well as "The Totally Sweet '90s." She's been a journalist since 1989, working at Mpls.St.Paul Magazine, Twin Cities Sidewalk, the Minneapolis Star Tribune, and NBC News Digital. She's Gen X in birthdate, word and deed. If Marathon candy bars ever come back, she'll be first in line.

title: BlizzCon 2026: New Starcraft Shooter, Diablo 5, World of Warcraft Forever
snippet: News and trailers from Blizzard’s opening ceremony.
fullText:
In a packed, rowdy BlizzCon main hall, the game developer finally confirmed the rumors: We’re getting a shooter set in the Starcraft universe. The game is titled simply Starcraft.

All we saw was a brief teaser that showed the rise and sudden fall of an elite soldier. Still, Starcraft (the game) is the first major news from Starcraft (the series) in a decade, when Starcraft 2’s Nova Covert Ops campaign pack was released. The announcement of the franchise’s return rocked the enormous main hall at BlizzCon. 

I grew up playing the original Starcraft, spending late nights in custom games with friends, so I’m interested to see whether (and how) Blizzard can revitalize the franchise.

The game is planned for a 2030 launch, a full two decades after the release of StarCraft 2.

Diablo 5 announced, alongside Netflix series

In 2029, Sanctuary will finally fall. Players will fight to take it back in Diablo 5. 

In a dark and hazy main hall, Blizzard Entertainment showed a short teaser revealing Diablo’s return at the BlizzCon opening ceremony. For the series’ 30th anniversary, Diablo announced plans to drag players deeper into the darkness than they’ve ever seen. Diablo 5 will show us what happens when the Lord of Terror finally takes over the world. 

According to Diablo devs, the game will explore the question of what you must become to save a world that has already fallen. 

The past two Diablo games spent about a decade in development, so the announcement of the next entry is earlier than expected. We just wrapped the Mephisto storyline, and here comes Diablo announcing his (eventual) return. 

In the meantime, there’s still more planned for Diablo 4, which released its Lord of Hatred expansion earlier this spring. Blizzard will add the Amazon class — a returning favorite from Diablo 2 — via a class pack next year. It’s not a full expansion, but it gives players the opportunity to explore the Skovos Isles, home of the Amazons, as one of their own.

Blizzard CEO Johanna Faries also announced that an animated Diablo series is coming to Netflix and hinted that there may be more planned for other franchises sometime in the future.

World of Warcraft is forever, and Forever comes in November

The rumored “Classic plus” is coming to Blizzard’s flagship MMO. Titled World of Warcraft Forever, the game will funnel new content to players while preserving the feel (and level cap) of vanilla WoW.  

WoW Forever will add three new zones, overhaul several existing zones, drop 1,000 new quests into the game alongside nine new dungeons, two new raids and a new Skyborne race. 

Perhaps most surprisingly, the beta for WoW Forever opens on Thursday, and the game is set for a launch in less than two months, on Nov. 4.

Over in contemporary WoW, the latest expansion, Midnight, is entering the next phase of its story. Blizzard showed us a new cinematic that raised the stakes in ways that, as a non-WoW player, I frankly didn’t really follow, but it looked momentous. 

We also got a tease for the next expansion, The Last Titan, which will conclude the Worldsoul trilogy of expansions that began with 2024’s The War Within. 

Alongside a 3.0 update to Warcraft 3: Reforged, a remaster of the classic real-time strategy game, Blizzard is releasing a new Forsaken Kingdom campaign, launching today.

Overwatch finally reworked Roadhog and Sombra (again)

Blizzard’s hero shooter had its big moment earlier this year, when the game announced 10 new heroes for its 10th anniversary, plus a new, ongoing story that has spanned everything from cinematics to in-game map changes. The game’s BlizzCon announcements weren’t as big as those of other franchises, but there were still some surprises tucked away.

We got our first look at Doctrine, a vampire-inspired support hero who will join the roster in season 5 next month. Doctrine is playable this weekend in a hero preview before joining the roster permanently in October.

The game is also adding a new escort map, set in the Icelandic prison that contained Doctrine before Doomfist and his crew of ex-Talon members broke him out. 

A new support hero and a new map were expected. What really made me shoot forward in my seat was the announcement that hero reworks are starting to come through — and longtime damage hero Sombra is switching roles and becoming a support hero. 

Sombra’s been a tough nut to crack for Overwatch, often overpowered at the highly coordinated pro level, and annoying to both teammates and opponents at the casual level — largely due to her ability to go invisible and quickly teleport across the map. She’s already been through four reworks by my count, and the devs seem to make smaller-but-still-substantial tweaks to her kit every six months or so. As a longtime support player and Sombra-enjoyer (which I will not apologize for), I’m very excited for this change.

Roadhog’s also getting a rework, although he’s staying within the tank role. Like Sombra, he’s a hero who’s been a longtime annoyance for players, due largely to being balanced around a hook ability that can quickly combo down non-tank heroes.

Hearthstone announces next expansion, new class coming next year

Blizzard’s card battler is taking players back 10,000 years in the past with the upcoming Reign of the Black Empire expansion, which adds a new “assemble” keyword allowing players to smush two minions’ text boxes together. It’s also getting a new Journey feature that will be a dedicated home for events, story content and limited-time events.

In March, the game will also add its first new hero in six years: the monk. Blizzard didn’t say much about the new class, but I’m sure we’ll hear more about it over the course of BlizzCon.

New content for Heroes of the Storm

Heroes of the Storm is getting a new hero for the first time in six years. Xal’atath from World of Warcraft is joining the roster later this month. The multiplayer online battle arena has been largely in maintenance mode since 2022, though still receiving periodic balance patches. Whether the new hero marks the start of more dedicated support for the game likely depends on how much interest it generates.

 

This is a developing story and will be updated as Blizzard releases more information.

Editors’ note: Adam Benjamin’s travel costs for BlizzCon were covered by Blizzard Entertainment. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

title: Apple nailed iPhone Duo split screen, even as iPad multitasking feels convoluted
snippet: Apple this week unveiled its new iPhone lineup, including the first ever foldable iPhone – the iPhone Duo. While the Duo itself is a fantastic device, it does leave me wishing that Apple did better for the iPad. more…
fullText:
Apple this week unveiled its new iPhone lineup, including the first ever foldable iPhone – the iPhone Duo. While the Duo itself is a fantastic device, it does leave me wishing that Apple did better for the iPad.

Ever since the release of iPadOS 26 last year, I’ve missed the earlier days of iPad multitasking. Sure, windowing is cool – but I don’t want that all the time. With iPadOS 26, you’re either all in on windowing, or you can only use apps in full screen. Apple did re-introduce split screen and slideover in later versions, but the features still require you to utilize the windowing system.

With iPhone Duo, multitasking feels much more elegant. You can put an app into half of a splitscreen, whilst still seeing your full home screen to select another app. You can also save apps as a pair for swapping into later. iPhone Duo also offers something no iPad offers, the ability to splitscreen a video with an app. On iPad mini, which is very similarly sized to iPhone Duo, this could be excellent.

And yet, iPadOS 27 still takes an all or nothing approach to multitasking. Even on the iPad mini where windowing is far too convoluted.

	

iPhone Duo offers a vision for how nice multitasking could be on the iPad. I’m not saying we should take away windowing, but if Apple has already engineered a simpler multitasking system, why not bring it to the iPad. At its core, iPadOS is still iOS, and while not everything can automatically scale to the iPad, it shouldn’t be a massive undertaking.

Personally, I’m incredibly excited for the iPhone Duo. Apple nailed the software implementation in a manner that nobody was really thinking about, but in hindsight its such an obvious direction for the future of foldables. I just wish Apple didn’t make iPad multitasking borderline hostile towards those of us who aren’t using a Magic Keyboard.

title: iPhone Duo can add fake bezel to the outside screen for better case compatibility
snippet: Blogger Nicolas Lellouche went digging in the iPhone Duo settings during his hands on time with the device. He found a curious new option in the display settings called ‘Shift Left Edge’. When enabled, this setting adds a bit of a black border to the left side, essentially adding fake bezel on the outside screen, pushing content away from the folding edge. more…
fullText:
Blogger Nicolas Lellouche went digging in the iPhone Duo settings during his hands on time with the device. He found a curious new option in the display settings called ‘Shift Left Edge’. 

When enabled, this setting adds a bit of a black border to the left side, essentially adding fake bezel on the outside screen, pushing content away from the folding edge.

The description for this setting in the iPhone Duo software says that it “moves content when you are using a case that partially covers the left edge of the outer display of your iPhone”.

As you can see from his short demo video, with the setting turned on, it roughly doubles the width of the black border on the left edge of the iPhone’s Duo outer screen. 

It’s unclear what kind of cases would require this setting to be enabled. 

Apple is offering two first-party case accessories for the iPhone Duo at launch; the iPhone Duo Case and the iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand. 

Without having proper hands on time, it’s hard to tell whether these cases significantly overlap the left edge and obscure the screen content, but it doesn’t seem like it would be an issue. It is possible Apple is envisaging this setting will be useful for other — perhaps more rugged — case designs offered by third-party accessory makers.

We’ll know more closer to launch. iPhone Duo goes on sale next month, on October 23rd.

title: Volkswagen’s crazy-efficient EV borrows an idea from Slate
snippet: Volkswagen's new efficiency-minded halo car is almost twice as efficient as the most efficient production car, the Lucid Air.
fullText:
Volkswagen took the covers off a new prototype electric vehicle Monday, one that’s capable of hitting the equivalent of 323 miles per gallon under ideal conditions, making it one of the most efficient cars in the world.

It’s not unusual for automakers to float pie-in-the-sky concepts with outlandish stats, but Volkswagen took it a step or two further by building the EV and driving it from its home base in Wolfsburg, Germany, on a 794-mile (1,278-kilometer) trip to Vienna. The team charged the Mission Efficiency prototype once during the journey and arrived with 104 miles (168 kilometers) of range left, resulting in consumption of 7.51 kilowatt-hours per 100 miles, or about 279 MPGe.

Volkswagen actually built and drove the Mission Efficiency prototypeImage Credits:Volkswagen

The teardrop-shaped Mission Efficiency prototype was built using the electric motor and battery from the ID. Polo, two features that bring the car to “near production” status, Volkswagen said in a press release. 

For those keeping score, the prototype is almost twice as efficient as the most efficient production car in the world, the Lucid Air Pure. 

By some back-of-the-envelope math, Volkswagen’s science experiment can get more than 400 miles of range out of a 54.9-kilowatt-hour battery, though that’s not an official EPA rating. Lucid gets 420 miles from an 84-kilowatt-hour battery per EPA ratings, but it’s a much larger and more practical vehicle. 

Volkswagen had to make some compromises in the name of efficiency.

The most noticeable is the roofline, which tapers quickly after peaking above the driver’s head. The shape, known as a Kammback, is among the most aerodynamic shapes a vehicle can take. Volkswagen was able to bring the coefficient of drag down to 0.158, while also keeping the frontal area low at just 2.08 square meters. 

Being a 2+2, the Mission Efficiency’s back seat is suitable for children, maybeImage Credits:Volkswagen

As a result, the Mission Efficiency is technically a 2+2, meaning the rear seats aren’t suitable for most adults. Volkswagen said the backseat is designed for people shorter than 5-foot 3 inches, or about 1.6 meters. 

“The prototype was designed so that it could theoretically be used by a young family of four,” Volkswagen said, though anyone who has contemplated sitting in a 2+2 knows that even kids might scoff at the notion.

Another compromise sits closer to the road. Because wheels and tires can contribute about a quarter to a third of aerodynamic drag, the designers tightened the space between the wheel arches and the front tires. It’s great for efficiency, but probably not great for ride quality since wheels need space to move inside the wheel wells so the shocks can absorb bumps.

Volkswagen included some clever touches, including this storage bin that’s hidden behind the rear wheel coverImage Credits:Volkswagen

One place Volkswagen didn’t compromise was the mirrors. Sideview mirrors generate a lot of drag just by hanging off the sides, and while cameras would have cut into those losses significantly, they don’t offer the same sense of depth that true mirrors do. 

To top it all off, Volkswagen put solar cells on the roof and the trunk lid. It’s a nice touch that’s sure to delight the internet, but their impact is limited, adding just 18 miles (30 kilometers) to perfectly flat, sunny routes driven at a constant 42.25 mph (68 kph).

Like the Slate EV pickup, the Mission Efficiency doesn’t come with an infotainment systemImage Credits:Volkswagen

Inside, the seats are built using lightweight materials and designs. On the dash, Volkswagen took a page from EV startup Slate Auto. Like Slate’s bare-bones pickup, the Mission Efficiency doesn’t come with an infotainment system or built-in speakers. Instead, it offers a portable Bluetooth speaker and assumes drivers will bring their own devices.

While Volkswagen frequently calls the Mission Efficiency a “near production” vehicle, the company didn’t commit to actual production. Though don’t assume it won’t: Over a decade ago, the automaker produced 250 examples of the XL1, another efficiency-minded halo car. And like other halo cars, it didn’t come cheap, with prices starting at €110,000 in 2013.

De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism.
